## Summary
- Add Prompt Input system design document (`design/gdd/prompt-input.md`), the 12th of 15 planned systems
- Define the **three-column layout specification** for the Match scene (left ~20% / center ~60% / right ~20%) that persists across all match phases (SETUP → PLAYING → FINISHED)
- Design **turn-based prompt input flow**: P1 writes on the left panel → Ready → P2 writes on the right panel → Ready → auto-countdown
- Update `systems-index.md` progress to 11/14 MVP systems designed

## Details
Key design decisions made during this GDD:
- **Turn-based input** (not simultaneous) — realistic for single-keyboard local play
- **Side panels** (P1 left, P2 right) — maze stays fully visible and unobstructed in center
- **API config in external files** — Prompt Input focuses solely on prompt text collection
- **Placeholder example prompt** — guides new players without constraining creativity
- **Dual-Ready auto-countdown** — symmetric, ceremonial, matches competitive feel

The three-column layout established here is the visual framework that Match Renderer (#11), Match HUD (#13), and Result Screen (#14) will reuse in their respective match phases.

author: carlos-alm
body:
## Summary

- **Query benchmark**: Fix ENOENT from doubled file paths on CI. The `benchDiffImpact` function reads `row.file` from the DB and joins it with the repo root, but on CI the npm-installed `buildGraph` (v3.8.0) stores paths that include the root directory prefix without a leading `/` — producing paths like `/root/root/src/...`. Add `resolveDbFile()` helper that detects absolute-like paths and falls back to prepending `/` when the joined path doesn't exist. Also adds a diagnostic log + graceful fallback instead of crashing the entire worker.

- **Embedding benchmark**: Increase per-model timeout from 10→20 minutes and add explicit workflow timeout (180 min). On cold CI caches, model downloads alone can exceed the 10-minute timeout, causing all 7 models to silently fail.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify query benchmark passes locally (`node --experimental-strip-types --import ./scripts/ts-resolve-loader.js scripts/query-benchmark.ts --version dev`)
- [ ] Trigger benchmark workflow via `workflow_dispatch` and confirm query-benchmark job succeeds

author: prjanitor
body:
## Bug Description

The `num_features` parameter in `BatchNorm1D` defaults to `None`, which causes PyTorch's `BatchNorm1d` to raise an error when instantiated without this required parameter.

## Root Cause

The validation logic only checked if `num_features` was an integer when it was not None:
```python
if num_features is not None and not isinstance(num_features, int):
    raise ValueError("Please provide a valid num_features")
```

This allowed `num_features=None` to pass validation, but PyTorch requires this parameter.

## Fix

Changed the validation to also check for `None`:
```python
if num_features is None or not isinstance(num_features, int):
    raise ValueError("Please provide a valid num_features")
```

## Testing

Users will now receive a clear error message when attempting to create a `BatchNorm1D` layer without specifying `num_features`.

author: mergify[bot]
body:
## Why I'm doing

For ARRAY/MAP/STRUCT default values, `DefaultValueColumnIterator::init()` constructs a `Datum` via **placement new** into MemPool-allocated memory (`default_value_column_iterator.cpp`). However, `MemPool` only frees raw bytes without calling destructors, so the `Datum`'s internal heap-allocated containers (`std::vector<Datum>`, `std::map<DatumKey, Datum>`) were never destroyed, causing memory leaks.

## What I'm doing

- Add `~DefaultValueColumnIterator()` that explicitly calls `Datum::~Datum()` for ARRAY/MAP/STRUCT types before MemPool reclaims the raw memory
- Add unit tests covering ARRAY, MAP, and STRUCT default value iterator lifecycle to catch regressions under ASAN

Fixes: https://github.com/StarRocks/StarRocksTest/issues/11198

<!--

Thank you for contributing to DeepFlow!
Please read this template before submitting pull requests.
Texts surrounded by `<` and `>` should be replaced accordingly.
Put an `x` in `[ ]` to mark the item as checked. `[x]`

-->

### This PR is for:

- Agent

### Fixes incorrect `close_type=9` classification for successful L7 requests that are closed by client RST, including both late cached L7 stats and
  `ForcedReport` merge cases

#### Steps to reproduce the bug
  - Enable normal managed-mode L4 and L7 collection on the agent.
  - Send a short-lived HTTP probe request and let the server return a normal `200 OK` response.
  - Close the client connection immediately with RST after the response is received.
  - Observe that `l7_flow_log` reports a successful response, while `l4_flow_log` may still classify the same connection as `close_type=9`.
  - In some paths, the successful L7 result is still buffered in the cache when the final close type is calculated.
  - In other paths, the L7 success is first recorded in an intermediate `ForcedReport` flow and then merged with a later final close event that is still
  marked as client reset.

#### Changes to fix the bug
  - Merge cached L7 performance stats into the flow before the final `update_close_type()` decision, so late-arriving successful L7 responses can affect
  the final close classification.
  - Reuse the already collected cached L7 stats during the end-of-flow flush path to avoid losing them after the cache pop.
  - Reconcile `close_type` again during `Flow::sequential_merge()` so flows that already contain successful L7 responses from an earlier `ForcedReport`
  are reclassified from `TcpClientRst` to `TcpFinClientRst` after the final merge.
  - Keep the original client-reset classification when the merged L7 stats contain client-side or server-side error signals.
  - Add regression tests for both the cached-L7 close-type path and the `ForcedReport` merge path.
#### Affected branches
- main
- v7.1
- v6.6

- [ ] Verified eBPF program runs successfully on linux 4.19.x.
- [ ] Verified eBPF program runs successfully on linux 5.2.x.

## Motivation In overlap scheduling, the backup of decode tokens within the `prepare_for_decode` method currently requires waiting for the forward stream to complete, resulting in significant CPU bubbles. This PR shifts the timing of the backup operation to occur at the conclusion of the forward pass, and verifies whether the backup is complete just prior to the commencement of the next forward iteration. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant S as Scheduler participant C as HiSparseCoordinator participant P as Decode Producer Stream participant B as Decode Backup Stream S->>C: map_last_loc_to_buffer(...) C->>C: prepare previous-token backup metadata C->>B: enqueue backup work Note over B: Backup is queued immediately
but waits on forward_done_event C->>C: grow device buffer / remap reserved slot P->>C: wait_for_pending_backup() Note over P,C: Before each decode pass,
wait for the previous backup to finish C-->>P: clear pending_backup_done_event P->>P: run decode forward P->>C: note_decode_forward_done() C->>C: record decode_forward_done_event B->>B: wait(decode_forward_done_event) B->>B: host_locs = alloc(...) ## 🔒 Pin GitHub Actions to commit SHAs

This PR pins all GitHub Actions to their exact commit SHA instead of mutable tags or branch names.

**Why?**
Pinning to a SHA prevents supply chain attacks where a tag (e.g. `v4`) could be moved to point to malicious code.

### Changes

| Workflow | Action | Avant | Après | SHA |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pypi-release.yml` | `actions/checkout` | `v6` | `v6.0.2` | `de0fac2e4500…` |
| `pypi-release.yml` | `actions/setup-python` | `v6` | `v6` | `a309ff8b426b…` |
| `pypi-release.yml` | `actions/github-script` | `v8` | `v8` | `ed597411d8f9…` |
| `trufflehog.yml` | `actions/checkout` | `v6` | `v6.0.2` | `de0fac2e4500…` |
| `trufflehog.yml` | `trufflesecurity/trufflehog` | `main` | `main` | `6bd2d14f7a4b…` |

Closes huggingface/tracking-issues#94

> **Low Risk**

author: copilot
body:
The backtesting engine had no intrinsic-value settlement at expiry, no assignment simulation for short ITM legs, and a hard-coded per-contract commission scalar. This PR introduces the core lifecycle hardening required for realistic options backtesting.

## New modules

- **`backtest/expiry.py`** — intrinsic-value settlement engine. Handles all leg polarities (long/short, call/put), assignment detection, and structure-aware payoff helpers:
  - `settle_legs_at_expiry()` — general multi-leg settler
  - `settle_vertical_spread`, `settle_iron_condor`, `settle_butterfly`, `settle_strangle`

- **`backtest/commission.py`** — `CommissionConfig` with three models: `PER_CONTRACT`, `PER_TRADE`, `HYBRID`, plus a `min_commission` floor. `from_legacy_rate()` bridges existing callsites.

## Updated modules

- **`lifecycle.py`** — adds `ExpiryLiquidationPolicy` enum (`LIQUIDATE_BEFORE_EXPIRY` | `SETTLE_AT_EXPIRY`) and embeds `CommissionConfig` into `LifecycleConfig`. Legacy `commission_per_contract` scalar is kept and synced via `__post_init__`.

- **`portfolio.py`** — open/close now route through `calculate_commission()`; new `expiry_settle_position()` settles a position at intrinsic value, correctly credits/debits cash, and stamps `assignment_occurred` + `settlement_notes` onto the `TradeRecord`.

- **`engine.py`** — `_process_exits` branches on policy:
  - `LIQUIDATE_BEFORE_EXPIRY` → existing force-close / expiry-close path (default, backward-compatible)
  - `SETTLE_AT_EXPIRY` → positions run to expiry and are settled via `expiry_settle_position()`

## Config

`config/rlm.yaml` gains `lifecycle` and `commission` sections:

```yaml
lifecycle:
  expiry_liquidation_policy: liquidate_before_expiry  # or settle_at_expiry
  force_close_dte: 1

commission:
  model: per_contract   # per_contract | per_trade | hybrid
  per_contract_rate: 0.65
  per_trade_rate: 0.0
  min_commission: 0.0
```

## Example: settlement path

```python
from rlm.backtest.expiry import settle_iron_condor

result = settle_iron_condor(
    long_put_strike=80, short_put_strike=90,
    short_call_strike=110, long_call_strike=120,
    underlying_price=115,  # short call breached
    contract_multiplier=100,
)
# result.cash_impact == -500.0, result.assignment_occurred == True
```

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

# Mission: Implement Phase 1 - Realism and Correctness

Take the current `DGator86/Regime-Locus-Matrix` repository and begin hardening it by addressing the most critical realism gaps in the backtesting engine.

## Phase 1 Objectives:

### 1. Implement Expiry and Settlement Realism

The current backtesting logic is too naive around option expiration. This phase must introduce robust handling for all scenarios related to an option's final moments.

**Requirements:**
- **Forced Close Logic:** Add logic to force the closure of positions nearing expiration (e.g., DTE <= 1). This should be a configurable policy.
- **Settlement at Expiry:** Implement correct P&L calculation for options held through expiration.
  - **Intrinsic Value Settlement:** Expiring ITM (In-The-Money) options must settle based on their intrinsic value.
  - **Long/Short Leg Handling:** Differentiate between long and short options at expiry. Long OTM options expire worthless. Short OTM options expire worthless (full profit).
  - **Vertical Spreads:** Correctly resolve the payoff for vertical spreads (debit and credit) at expiry based on the settlement of both legs.
  - **Complex Structures:** Implement payoff resolution for Condors, Butterflies, and Strangles.
- **Assignment/Exercise Simulation:** For any short ITM leg, simulate assignment and its impact on the portfolio's cash balance. This is critical for realistic risk modeling.
- **Expiration-Day Liquidation Policy:** Add a configurable toggle to either hold through expiry or liquidate all positions on the final trading day.

### 2. Add Commissions and Lifecycle Costs

Introduce a configurable commission model to account for transaction costs.

**Requirements:**
- **Commission Model:** Implement a flexible commission structure (e.g., per-contract, per-trade, or a hybrid).
- **Lifecycle Cost Application:** Apply commissions on trade entry and exit. Ensure this is reflected in the final P&L.

## Target Modules for Implementation:

Based on the spec, the following new and updated files are the primary targets for this phase:
- `src/rlm/backtest/lifecycle.py` (New or heavily updated)
- `src/rlm/backtest/expiry.py` (New)
- `src/rlm/backtest/commission.py` (New)
- `src/rlm/backtest/portfolio.py` (Update to integrate new logic)
- `src/rlm/backtest/engine.py` (Update to orchestrate new components)
- `configs/base.yaml` (Update with new configuration toggles for expiry and commissions)

## Acceptance Criteria for this Phase:

- Open positions are handled correctly through expiry without surviving unrealistically.
- P&L at expiry accurately reflects intrinsic value settlement for all supported option structures.
- A configurable commission model is in place and correctly impacts backtest results.
- The system can differentiate between holding-to-expiry and pre-expiry liquidation policies.
- Unit and integration tests are added to validate the correctness of the new expiry payoff logic.

The following is the prior conversation context from the user's chat exploration (may be truncated):

User: Use this as the master handoff spec for the coding agent. It is written to drive implementation, not discussion.

⸻

Take the current DGator86/Regime-Locus-Matrix repository from a strong research-grade regime/options framework to a hardened, integration-ready subsystem that can plug into the broader trading architecture.

This is not a greenfield build. The repo already contains:
	•	factor pipeline

body:
When we are at the appointment details page, and have the option allow_guests turned on, and go to the editor for translation, we encounter the issue.
Steps To Reproduce:
1. Create an appointment.
2. Go to the "Options" tab, and click on "Allow Guests".
3. Go to the web page for the appointment, select the data and time.
4. Now, on the details page, go to any other language than the default, and click on edit/translate.
5. The issue occurs.

The issue occurs when the regex tries to match the placeholder where the guests are added, which is enabled by the allow_guests. It contains strings  with newline characters. The regex fails to take into consideration for these newlines and breaks causing the issue to appear.

To fix the issue, we'll use regex to account for the new lines.

author: creatorrmode-lead
body:
## Summary

Adds **Agent Veil Protocol** to the **Identity & Trust** section.

AVP is an off-chain EigenTrust compute layer for ERC-8004 — it computes graph-based trust scores with Sybil detection and collusion resistance, then returns signed attestations with Merkle proofs that agents write to ReputationRegistry via `giveFeedback()` using their own wallet. AVP holds no wallet and pays no gas.

- **SDK**: [pypi.org/project/agentveil](https://pypi.org/project/agentveil/) (`pip install agentveil`)
- **GitHub**: [github.com/creatorrmode-lead/avp-sdk](https://github.com/creatorrmode-lead/avp-sdk)
- **Bridge endpoint**: `GET /v1/bridge/erc8004/{did}/attestation`
- **Site**: [agentveil.dev](https://agentveil.dev)

## Why Identity & Trust section

AVP provides the trust computation layer that ERC-8004 intentionally leaves open — reputation aggregation, Sybil resistance, and dispute resolution on top of raw on-chain feedback.

Integrated with [Microsoft Agent Governance Toolkit](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-governance-toolkit/pull/1010) as official TrustProvider.

body: ## Summary This PR adds stateless MCP client support to the Playground. Fixes #1434 Previously, the Playground always assumed MCP routes should use the legacy SSE transport (`/sse`). That broke connections for routes backed by `statefulMode: stateless`, which should use streamable HTTP on `/mcp`. ## What changed - detect MCP backend `statefulMode` from the selected route - use `/mcp` with `StreamableHTTPClientTransport` for stateless MCP routes - keep using `/sse` with `SSEClientTransport` for stateful MCP routes - update displayed connection endpoint to show the actual MCP transport URL - show MCP session mode (`STATEFUL` / `STATELESS`) in the connection panel - update MCP connection error messages to reference the actual transport URL instead of always assuming `/sse` ## Why Stateless MCP backends are expected to use the streamable HTTP transport. The previous Playground behavior caused connection failures such as `405 Method Not Allowed` because it still tried to POST through the SSE path. ## Reproduction A stateless MCP route like the following failed to connect from the Playground before this change: ```yaml backends: - mcp: statefulMode: stateless targets: - name: mcp-poc mcp: host: http://localhost:8082/mcp ``` ## Testing - ran npm run build in ui - verified the UI build succeeds - confirmed the Playground now selects /mcp for stateless MCP routes and /sse for stateful MCP routes

## 🔒 Pin GitHub Actions to commit SHAs

This PR pins all GitHub Actions to their exact commit SHA instead of mutable tags or branch names.

Pinning to a SHA prevents supply chain attacks where a tag (e.g. `v4`) could be moved to point to malicious code.

body:
## Why

The web explorer had no way to see what events had actually been published across domains. Debugging event-driven workflows meant adding puts statements or inspecting the Ruby REPL — there was no browser-visible event history.

## What changed

- **`EventIntrospector`** — reads a merged event bus and exposes `all_entries`, `event_types`, `aggregate_types` with optional type/aggregate filtering
- **`events.erb`** — filterable HTML table at `/events` with type badge, aggregate name, timestamp, and expandable payload `<details>` toggle; empty state when no events published
- **`MultiDomainServer`** — `MergedEventBus` struct, `require event_introspector`, Events nav link, `/events` route dispatch
- **`MultiDomainUIRoutes#serve_events`** — merges all runtime event buses, builds introspector, renders the events page

## URL

```
GET /events                            # all events, newest first
GET /events?type=PizzaCreated          # filter by event type
GET /events?aggregate=Pizza            # filter by aggregate
GET /events?type=PizzaCreated&aggregate=Pizza
```

## Specs

- `event_introspector_spec.rb` — 9 examples: filtering, ordering, edge cases
- `event_log_route_spec.rb` — 3 rendering examples using stub_const fake events

Supersedes #203 (conflict resolution).

author: davidor
body:
### What does this PR do?

This PR fixes a bug in the entity completeness detection code in workloadmeta.

The code incorrectly assumed that when running on Kubernetes, pod entity information comes from two sources: the node orchestrator and the cluster orchestrator. This is true for the Node Agent, but not for the Cluster Agent. In the Cluster Agent, there's a single collector for pods: kubeapiserver. As a result, pods in the Cluster Agent were always marked as incomplete.

This bug doesn't impact any functionality because completeness information is not yet used in the Cluster Agent. But it could be in the future, so it needs to be fixed.


### Describe how you validated your changes

New unit tests. Also, deployed locally with some debug logs in the tagger to verify that pods in the Cluster Agent are now reported as complete.

author: simoncqk
body:
See design doc plan: #402 

Changes: 

Add GPU Direct RDMA (GDR) support to 3FS usrbio, enabling direct data transfers between storage and GPU vRAM without host memory bounce buffers.

  ### API

  - New `_device` API variants: `hf3fs_iovcreate_device`, `hf3fs_iovopen_device`, `hf3fs_iovwrap_device`
  - `iovcreate_device` always available with transparent host fallback; `iovopen_device`/`iovwrap_device`
  require `HF3FS_GDR_ENABLED`
  - `hf3fs_iovsync(iov, direction)` for GPU↔NIC coherency fencing
  - Runtime capability queries: `hf3fs_gdr_available()`, `hf3fs_gdr_device_count()`, `hf3fs_iov_mem_type()`
  - Existing host API unchanged and fully backward compatible

  ### RDMA Layer

  - `RDMABufAccelerator` for GPU memory RDMA registration via `nvidia_peermem`
  - `RDMABufUnified` as polymorphic host/GPU RDMA buffer abstraction
  - `AcceleratorMemoryRegionCache` for MR caching with per-device eviction
  - `AcceleratorMemoryBridge` for cross-process CUDA IPC import/export
  - `IBSocket::RDMAReqBatch::add()` and `CallContext::RDMATransmission::add()` overloads for
  `RDMABufUnified`

  ### StorageClient

  - `IOBuffer` wraps `RDMABufUnified` instead of plain `RDMABuf`
  - Inline data transfer automatically disabled for GPU buffers
  - Client-side CPU checksum automatically skipped for GPU buffers
  - `registerGpuIOBuffer()` with fallback to `RDMABuf::createFromUserBuffer`

  ### Fuse Daemon

  - `IovTable` parses `.gdr.d{N}` symlink keys and `gdr://v1/device/{id}/size/{size}/ipc/{hex}` URIs
  - `GpuShmBuf`/`GpuShmBufForIO` for daemon-side imported GPU buffer management
  - `IoBufForIO` = `std::variant<ShmBufForIO, GpuShmBufForIO>` with `std::visit` dispatch in
  `IoRing::process()`
  - `lookupBufs` two-phase locking: `shmLock` then `gpuShmLock` (never nested)

  ### Build & Infra

  - `cmake/Cuda.cmake` for CUDA toolkit detection and `HF3FS_GDR_ENABLED` flag
  - CI workflow updated for optional GDR build matrix

  ### Docs

  - `docs/gdr-integration.md`: user-facing guide with prerequisites, API reference, 3 complete usage
  examples, runtime behavior, and known limitations

author: zbigniewsobiecki
body:
## Summary

Fixes a 7-minute session freeze caused by LLMs (Gemini Flash Preview) generating colon-separated
dependencies instead of comma-separated ones in gadget headers.

**Root cause chain:**
1. LLM writes `!!!GADGET_START:RunCommand:create_folder:create_folder:parent_folder` (colons between deps)
2. Parser only reads `parts[2]` as deps → `parts[3]` (the real dep) silently dropped
3. Parser sees invocation ID as only dep → false self-referential dependency
4. Dispatcher skips entire gadget → LLM degenerates into 65K tokens of repeated base64 garbage
5. No stream timeout → session hangs for 7 minutes

**Three fixes:**
- **Parser resilience**: `parts.slice(2).join(",")` captures all deps regardless of separator, with deduplication
- **Self-referential filtering**: filter out only self-ref deps, keep valid ones (single-pass partition)
- **In-flight timeout**: configurable `inFlightTimeoutMs` (default 300s) with `gadget_skipped` events for timed-out gadgets

## Test plan

- [x] 5 new parser tests (colon-separated deps, mixed separators, dedup)
- [x] 4 new dispatcher self-ref tests (filter+execute, filter+queue, all-self-ref skip, dup self-refs)
- [x] 4 new timeout tests (skip events, normal completion, default timeout, no in-flight)
- [x] Full regression: 5983 tests pass, 0 type errors
- [x] Biome lint clean on all changed files

# Description

Based on #3022, this commit enables the BWD_D direction for f32 `jit:sve_128` and `jit_1x1:sve_128` convolutions. It also makes certain deconvolution shapes (width-only, unit height) use the `conv:any+jit:sve_128` implementation over `acl`, leading to significant speedups.

Support for the BWD_W direction was also added for both JIT paths, but they remain unselected because of a few observed regressions for small shapes with 1x1 kernel at 64/96 threads.

## Performance improvements (f32)
The following conv shape batches were benchmarked on a c8g instance, at various thread counts (1/4/16/64/96) in BWD_D direction:

- `shapes_resnet_50`
- `shapes_yolo_v2`
- `shapes_mobilenet`
- `shapes_efficientdet`

### What this PR does / Why we need it?

Adds internal retry logic (3 attempts, exponential backoff) to SFTP credential fetching and file upload in the mustgather investigation, so transient failures are handled locally without re-running the expensive must-gather.

If local retries are exhausted, `InfrastructureError` wrapping is preserved as a fallback for the controller-level retry.

body:
💡 What: Pre-computed stringified row representation outside the filter loop instead of calculating it dynamically inside the `is_match` function on every iteration.
🎯 Why: Applying multiple filters iteratively calculated string representations repeatedly, resulting in an O(num_filters * num_rows) bottleneck during parsing.
📊 Impact: Reduced large dataset processing time significantly (~90% time savings for string transformation overhead based on internal benchmark: 29s to 2.5s for 20k rows).
🔬 Measurement: Performance tested with local benchmarking script `benchmark_parse.py`, verified with standard test suite.

author: leburgeon
body:
This pull request introduces a major refactor to the Lambda chatbot backend and the Streamlit dashboard frontend to support robust asynchronous question processing, addressing API Gateway timeout limitations and improving user experience. The backend now dispatches questions as asynchronous jobs tracked in DynamoDB, while the frontend dashboard polls for completion. Additional improvements include better logging for debugging and filtering of relevant documents for RAG indexing.

**Asynchronous Job Processing (Lambda Backend):**
- Refactors `lambda_function.py` to support three modes: dispatching jobs (`POST /ask`), polling job status (`GET /status/{job_id}`), and running the actual RAG pipeline as a worker (async Lambda invocation). Job state and results are stored in DynamoDB with TTL for auto-cleanup. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-1f2723b89499aa9a255cca46487e32a381bb8c78a624805ce759bdcf063ce8f8L3-R13) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1f2723b89499aa9a255cca46487e32a381bb8c78a624805ce759bdcf063ce8f8R28-R43) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-1f2723b89499aa9a255cca46487e32a381bb8c78a624805ce759bdcf063ce8f8L104-R289) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-1f2723b89499aa9a255cca46487e32a381bb8c78a624805ce759bdcf063ce8f8L150-R346)
- Adds helper functions for storing and retrieving job records in DynamoDB, including error handling and TTL management. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-1f2723b89499aa9a255cca46487e32a381bb8c78a624805ce759bdcf063ce8f8R28-R43) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1f2723b89499aa9a255cca46487e32a381bb8c78a624805ce759bdcf063ce8f8L104-R289)

**Frontend Dashboard Integration:**
- Updates `dashboard/utils/chatbot.py` to use the new async job API: sends questions to `/ask`, then polls `/status/{job_id}` until completion, with configurable polling interval and timeout. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-459b03d6fd54f223dfffb8dadd4904891f83624ec762de3485127b9137d5304aR55-R69) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-459b03d6fd54f223dfffb8dadd4904891f83624ec762de3485127b9137d5304aR103-L112)
- Improves logging and endpoint configuration in `dashboard/app.py` for easier debugging and deployment. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ea8585cc482637297ded23c1672137835305d82aea8e223a8a8c3a9aede6e58bR13) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ea8585cc482637297ded23c1672137835305d82aea8e223a8a8c3a9aede6e58bR78-R88)

**Document Filtering for RAG Indexing:**
- Adds a `filter_relevant_documents` function in `extract_document_data.py` to select only relevant document types for RAG, and applies this filter in the PDF link extraction pipeline. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f7829e1f7bd09a36e284deee19b8dc6b72a153367dc4e166826ba18b0c5576bcR326-R354) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f7829e1f7bd09a36e284deee19b8dc6b72a153367dc4e166826ba18b0c5576bcL346-R384)

**Logging and Debugging Enhancements:**
- Adds detailed logging throughout the backend and frontend to trace job dispatch, status polling, and LLM queries, aiding observability and troubleshooting. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ba6221084b2a5348e90b93092b15fb06a019ff1b70c5a05b8cd3a4f2126f2c8dR14-R25) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-400a5f719b4739fd0bf88fd72e05ecdc5fb4c84657716c0687faa6b0bc6b599aL38-L45) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-ea8585cc482637297ded23c1672137835305d82aea8e223a8a8c3a9aede6e58bR13) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-ea8585cc482637297ded23c1672137835305d82aea8e223a8a8c3a9aede6e58bR78-R88)

**Other Improvements:**
- Cleans up redundant code and improves error messages and validation for required fields in API requests. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-1f2723b89499aa9a255cca46487e32a381bb8c78a624805ce759bdcf063ce8f8L75-R90) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1f2723b89499aa9a255cca46487e32a381bb8c78a624805ce759bdcf063ce8f8L150-R346)

These changes collectively enable the chatbot to reliably handle longer-running RAG jobs, provide real-time status to users, and ensure only relevant documents are indexed, all while improving maintainability and debuggability.

author: 30omda
body:
### 🎨 Palette: Improve contact form accessibility and interactivity

#### 💡 What
This PR enhances the **Contact** section of the DinoDiv landing page by improving both form accessibility and the interactivity of contact details.

#### 🎯 Why
The previous implementation relied solely on placeholders for form field identification, lacked proper ARIA associations for validation errors, and provided static text for email and WhatsApp, requiring users to manually copy/paste. These changes ensure the form is accessible to screen reader users and makes contacting the team effortless.

#### ♿ Accessibility & UX Improvements
- **Semantic Labels:** Replaced raw inputs with Shadcn UI `Input` and `Textarea` components, each explicitly linked to a `<Label>` via `id` and `htmlFor`.
- **Error States:** Validation errors are now associated with their respective inputs using `aria-describedby` and `aria-invalid`. Errors are wrapped in `role="alert"` containers to ensure they are announced immediately by assistive technologies.
- **Actionable Links:** Transformed static email and phone numbers into functional `mailto:` and `https://wa.me/` links.
- **Keyboard Navigation:** Added `focus-visible:ring-1` and `rounded` styles to ensuring clear focus indicators for keyboard users navigating the contact details.
- **Design Consistency:** Used `h-auto` on Shadcn components to maintain the original design's generous vertical padding (`py-3`) without layout shifts.

#### 📸 Before/After
Verification was performed using a Playwright script that confirmed:
1. All inputs are correctly labeled.
2. Form fields are accessible via tab order.
3. Contact links are correctly formatted and interactive.
4. Validation errors are programmatically linked to inputs.

A visual confirmation screenshot was captured during verification at `/home/jules/verification/contact_ux_improvement.png`.

author: gotnochill815-web
body:
### Summary

This PR addresses a runtime compatibility issue in ChemBERTa when using transformers >= 5.0.

While #4913 resolves the import-time failure, ChemBERTa still fails during initialization due to tokenizer incompatibility.

---

### Problem

`RobertaTokenizerFast.from_pretrained()` fails for legacy BPE tokenizers (e.g. `seyonec/PubChem10M_SMILES_BPE_60k`) with:

ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 1)

---

### Solution

Introduce a fallback mechanism:

* Attempt to load `RobertaTokenizerFast`
* Fallback to `RobertaTokenizer`

---

### Impact

* No breaking changes
* Maintains backward compatibility
* Enables ChemBERTa to run successfully with transformers >=5.0

---

### Notes

Tested locally in Colab with transformers 5.x.

Model initializes successfully using default tokenizer after fallback.

author: copilot
body:
## Summary

Fixes all 9 bugs identified in the previous research session on the inline `_YOLO_CLS` fallback in `train_trocr_yolo.py` (active when `ultralytics` is not installed).

## Changes

### Critical crashes (would abort on every inference call)

| # | Location | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `_Detect.forward` L398 | `_make_anchors` returns a `(anchors, strides)` tuple; old code passed it directly to `_dist2bbox` which called `.T` on the tuple → `AttributeError`. Unpacked the tuple. |
| 5 | `_Boxes` | Missing `__iter__` caused `TypeError` in `_extract_ocr_lines` loop. Added `__iter__` yielding single-box `_Boxes` views with 2-D `xyxy`/`conf` so `box.xyxy[0]` works. |

### Silent wrong output (boxes in wrong coordinates)

| # | Location | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | `_Detect.forward` L398 | Stride scaling was missing — decoded boxes were in grid-cell units, not pixels. Added `* strides.squeeze(-1)`. |
| 3 | `_nms_boxes` + `__call__` | NMS returned indices into the score-filtered sub-array but caller indexed the full anchor array → wrong boxes. Rewrote `_nms_boxes` to track and return original indices. |
| 4 | `__call__` | Raw image passed to model without resize/pad-to-multiples-of-32. Added letterbox preprocessing (PIL or pure-numpy fallback) and inverse-letterbox transform to map detected boxes back to original image coordinates. |

### Training/weight issues

| # | Location | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 6 | `_YOLO_CLS.train()` | Loss was hardcoded to `0.0`, so `best_loss` dropped to `0.0` after epoch 1 with random-init weights saved as "best". Replaced with proxy L2 loss over detection-head feature maps (real gradient, honest convergence), with a prominent NOTE directing users to `pip install ultralytics` for real detection quality. |
| 7 | `_YOLO_CLS.__init__` | `self._imgsz` attribute was missing (required by the new letterbox logic). Added with default `512` matching `YOLO_IMG_SIZE`. |

### Error handling

| # | Location | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 8 | `_build_lm_encoder` | Called `_AutoModel`/`_AutoTokenizer` without checking `_LM_AVAILABLE` → `NameError` when `transformers` is not installed. Added early `ImportError` guard. |

### Cosmetic

| # | Location | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 9 | `_DFL.__init__` | Non-standard `data[:] = _nn.Parameter(...)` replaced with idiomatic `data = x.view(...).clone()`. |

## Verification

- `ruff check train_trocr_yolo.py` — ✅ all checks passed  
- `ruff format --check train_trocr_yolo.py` — ✅ already formatted  
- `python -c "import ast; ast.parse(...)"` — ✅ AST parses cleanly  
- CodeQL scan — ✅ 0 alerts

author: fellowseb
body:
### Proposed changes

Implements chunk `Users can view a and navigate to a "Custom views" tab on entities pages` of the ["Custom views" feature](https://github.com/OpenCTI-Platform/opencti/issues/13389)

A custom view is a dashboard an administrator creates for a given entity type. This dashboard is then viewable (not editable) by "normal" users.

#### User journeys

* Case 1: given there is one Custom views in DB for a specific Entity Type (ex.: Intrusion-Set); a participating user with the correct feature flag will see a  new tab appear on the SDO page with the name of the custom view. Clicking on the tab reroutes the user to the custom view `path` (`/[slug]-[id-without-dashes]`) and displays its content.
* Case 2: given there are multiple Custom views in DB for a specific Entity Type (ex.: Intrusion-Set); a participating user with the correct feature flag will see a `Custom views` tab appear on the SDO page. Clicking on the tab displays a drop-down menu with an item per custom view. Clicking on the menu items reroutes the user to the custom view `path` (`/[slug]-[id-without-dashes]`) and displays its content.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a0688e0a-11d1-44b0-a9c0-2bc3ef3491d8 

#### Specs

Figma: https://www.figma.com/design/K2TFfOTI4MBgWzIyGT2AHV/Custom-views?node-id=119-150&t=y1ubGmkFiRj9H8fl-0
Notion: https://www.notion.so/filigran/New-TAB-with-a-custom-knowledge-view-2b18fce17f2a80f09a34db26a15ff8d1

#### Details

##### Frontend

* Created a `useTabWithDropDown` hook that returns two components separately, for case 2: the returned Tab and the DropDown. Seems a little awkward but I had to do that given returning either a Fragment or an array of both elements under the `<Tabs>` component lead to styles not applied to the Tab.
* Created types like `DashboardManifest` and `DashboardConfig` to be reused in all places using dashboards (Dashboards, Public Dashboards & Custom views)
* Adds translation keys for the `Custom view` string

##### Backend

Data model changes:
* Adds a `path` property to the custom view entity type and expose it in the API. This will be a concatenation of a slug (from the `name`) with its ID, and is used in the URL bar of the user, it's a path à la Notion that allows changing the name/slug while still being able to open an old link.
* Adds a `target_entity_type` to CustomView entities to tell which entities are concerned by this custom view

### Related issues

* Fixes https://github.com/OpenCTI-Platform/opencti/issues/13389

### Manual testing

Feature branch deployment available here : https://feat-issue-13389-2-c.octi.staging.filigran.io/ .
Use "feat-issue-13389-2-c" credentials in 1Password.

Connect as `customers@filigran.io`.

To test case 1: go to a `Campaign` page. You should see a single custom view tab.
To test case 2 go to a `Intrusion Set` page. You should see two custom views under a dropdown tab.

- [x] I wrote test cases for the relevant uses case (coverage and e2e)
- [ ] I added/update the relevant documentation (either on github or on notion)
- [x] Where necessary I refactored code to improve the overall quality

author: subotic
body:
## Motivation

Documentation was spread across 18+ files with the same information (crate structure, testing pyramid, Datastar patterns, env vars, dev commands) appearing in up to 5 places. Factual errors had accumulated (stale deployment status, wrong just commands, misleading islands description). Directory names didn't match crate names (`app/` for `dpe-web`, `demo/` for `mosaic-playground`). Eight TOC entries in the mdBook linked to nonexistent pages.

## Summary

- Establish `docs/src/` as the single source of truth for all content
- Reshape `CLAUDE.md`, `CONVENTIONS.md`, `REVIEW.md` into lightweight agent index files by phase
- Rename `modules/dpe/app` → `web` and `modules/mosaic/demo` → `playground` to match crate names
- Fix all factual errors, add `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`

## Key Changes

### Documentation consolidation
- Expand thin docs/ pages: `repo_structure.md`, `tech_stack.md`, `workflows.md`, `deployment.md`
- Move Datastar conventions into `architecture.md`, testing conventions into `testing-strategy.md`
- New `review-guidelines.md` with full review checklist and doc links
- New `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` so GitHub auto-fills the PR template
- Simplify `README.md` to entry point with GitHub Pages link

### Fix factual errors
- `docs.md`: "not yet deployed" → deployed via GitHub Pages
- `introduction.md`: "DaSCH's website" → "Mosaic component library", fix "resdearchers" typo
- `onboarding.md`: clarify islands vs SSR distinction
- `testing.md`: remove stale "still evaluating Playwright" note, fix nonexistent `just` commands
- `workflows.md`: fix wrong `just` commands to match actual justfile

### Reshape agent files
- `CLAUDE.md`: slimmed to overview + doc pointer table + dev workflow
- `CONVENTIONS.md`: work-phase reference card (keeps commit types + PR template inline)
- `REVIEW.md`: review-phase checklist with doc links
- `modules/dpe/CLAUDE.md`: removed duplicated sections, kept DPE-specific guidance
- `modules/mosaic/CLAUDE.md`: updated all `demo` references to `playground`

### Directory renames
- `modules/dpe/app` → `modules/dpe/web` (matches crate name `dpe-web`)
- `modules/mosaic/demo` → `modules/mosaic/playground` (matches crate name `mosaic-playground`)
- `modules/mosaic/demo_macro` → `modules/mosaic/playground_macro` (matches crate name `mosaic-playground-macro`)
- `.claude/skills/add-component-to-demo` → `add-component-to-playground`
- Documented crate-to-folder naming convention in `docs/src/repo_structure.md`
- Updated all references: Cargo.toml, justfile, CI workflows, Dockerfiles, skills, learnings, docs

## Challenges and Decisions

### Deduplication vs. agent convenience
**Problem:** Some duplication (commit types table, PR template) exists for good reason — agents need them inline without reading another file.
**Tried:** Moving everything to docs/ with only links in agent files.
**Solution:** Keep the commit types table and PR template inline in CONVENTIONS.md since agents need these during PR/commit creation. Everything else links to docs/.

### Crate-to-folder naming convention
**Problem:** Directory names (`app/`, `demo/`, `demo_macro/`) didn't match crate names (`dpe-web`, `mosaic-playground`, `mosaic-playground-macro`), causing confusion in documentation.
**Solution:** Rename directories to strip the module prefix from the crate name (e.g., `dpe-web` → `dpe/web`). Documented as convention: crate `{module}-{role}` lives in folder `{module}/{role}`.

## Gotchas
- The new architecture: `docs/src/` = source of truth, agent files = phase-specific indexes. When adding content, put it in docs/ and link from agent files.
- `SUMMARY.md` no longer has stub entries. If new sections are needed, create the `.md` file first, then add the TOC entry.
- Folder naming convention: crate `{module}-{role}` lives in `modules/{module}/{role}`. Underscores replace hyphens only for proc macro crates (Rust requirement).

## Test Plan
- [x] `just docs-build` passes (no broken links)
- [x] `cargo metadata` resolves all workspace members correctly
- [x] No empty `()` links in SUMMARY.md
- [x] No stale `mosaic/demo` or `dpe/app` references remain
- [x] All cross-references in agent files point to existing docs/ files

## Review Notes
Each commit is a logical unit — review them separately:
1. **docs**: all documentation consolidation, fixes, and reshaping
2. **refactor(dpe-web)**: rename `app/` → `web/` + all reference updates
3. **refactor(mosaic)**: rename `demo/` → `playground/`, `demo_macro/` → `playground_macro/` + all reference updates

body:
### Motivation
- Improve robustness of OCR for remote files by retrying with an uploaded blob when URL-based OCR fails due to file corruption or server errors. 
- Make paid-mode file handling consistent with form conventions and client/server expectations by supporting both `files` and `files[]` upload fields. 
- Allow API callers to pass `action` via query string and preserve the original AI raw response for a new "raw decision" UI flow.

### Description
- Updated `api-docs.php` to read `action` from `$_GET['action']` when not present in `$_POST` by setting `$action = trim((string)($_POST['action'] ?? ($_GET['action'] ?? '')));`.
- In `api-groq-paid.php` `handleAnalyzePaidAction` now accepts `files[]` as an alternative upload key and `requestAssistantReply`/paid request uses `formData.append('files[]', ...)` so uploaded files are passed correctly to the paid endpoint.
- Enhanced OCR fallback behavior in three client scripts: `app/telegram-ai-response-dialog.js`, `app/telegram-appdosc.js`, and `docs.js` to download the remote file blob and re-upload it to the OCR endpoint when URL-based OCR returns recoverable errors, and to construct a `File` fallback with a normalized name and MIME type.
- Added helper `parseOcrPayload` and retry logic in `app/telegram-ai-response-dialog.js` to parse OCR responses and retry via file upload when patterns like `E301` or `Input file corrupted` are detected.
- Added `extractTelegramAiResponseText` and `renderTelegramRawResponse` in `app/telegram-appdosc.js` to extract and render raw AI payloads, and switched the brief modal to show the unmodified AI response when the new "use new decision" path is used.
- Adjusted attachment/context population in `app/telegram-ai-response-dialog.js` to use `extractedForContext` for `context.attachedFiles` so attached-file metadata reflects extracted files.
- Refactored `docs.js` OCR helper to use a `runOcrRequest` wrapper, add URL-download-and-reupload fallback, and centralize error handling for OCR requests.

### Testing
- Ran JavaScript linters and unit tests with `npm run lint` and `npm test`, and they completed without errors.
- Performed PHP syntax checks with `php -l` on changed files and no parse errors were reported.
- Executed integration smoke tests that POSTed sample file URLs and local files to the OCR and paid endpoints, and retries via blob upload succeeded where URL OCR originally failed.

author: copilot
body:
Two CI pipelines were failing on `main` after recent dependency bumps: appserver tests broke due to Flask/SQLAlchemy incompatibility, and client tests + Docker build broke due to a TypeScript version mismatch with `@types/jqueryui`.

## Merged PRs (#117–128)
- **Python (appserver):** sendgrid 6.12.5, sentry-sdk 2.57.0, intervaltree 3.2.1, types-redis 4.6.0, types-requests 2.33.0
- **Python (statistical-enrichment / cache-invalidator):** mypy 1.20.0, gunicorn 25.3.0
- **npm (client):** codelyzer 6.0.2, jasmine-spec-reporter 7.0.0, @types/vis 4.21.27, @types/node 25.5.0

## CI fixes

### `flask-sqlalchemy` 2.5.1 → 3.0.5
`flask-sqlalchemy<3` imports the private `flask._app_ctx_stack` symbol removed in Flask 2.0. With Flask now at 3.1.3 this caused an `ImportError` at test collection time. `flask-sqlalchemy` 3.0.x supports Flask 2.2+ and SQLAlchemy 1.4.18+ (project is on SQLAlchemy 1.4.54).

### `@types/jqueryui` 1.12.24 → 1.12.21
`@types/jqueryui` 1.12.22+ uses template literal types (e.g. `` `ui-resizable-${ResizableHandleDirection}` ``) introduced in TypeScript 4.1. The project targets TypeScript ~3.8, which cannot even *parse* this syntax — `skipLibCheck: true` only skips type-checking `.d.ts` files, not parsing them. Pinning to 1.12.21 (last pre-template-literal release) restores compilation.

author: arjanassink1978
body:
## Problem
CI test failures: 3 out of 49 RestAssured tests fail intermittently

**Error:**
```
JSON path username doesn't match.
Expected: user
Actual: null
```

Tests:
- `AuthControllerIT.login_happyPath_returns200AndSuccessTrue`
- `AuthControllerIT.login_happyPath_responseMessageIsLoginSuccessful`
- `AuthControllerIntegrationTest.loginWithValidCredentials_shouldReturn200AndSuccessTrue`

## Root Cause
The `username` field in LoginResponse was not being included in the JSON response in certain conditions. RestAssured couldn't find the field and defaulted to `null`, causing the assertions to fail.

## Solution
Added `@JsonInclude(JsonInclude.Include.ALWAYS)` annotation to the `username` field in LoginResponse DTO to guarantee the field is always present in the JSON serialization, even when the value is `null`.

This ensures RestAssured can always find the field and properly deserialize it.

## Files Changed
- `backend/src/main/java/techchamps/io/dto/response/LoginResponse.java` - Added @JsonInclude annotation

author: patrickliu0077
body:
## Summary

Adds a cookbook showing how to build agents that have real-time world awareness using calibrated prediction market data. The cookbook uses the OpenAI Agents SDK and demonstrates:

1. **Dynamic instructions** — agent fetches fresh world state (~800 tokens) before each run
2. **Depth tools** — focused topic drilling (`?focus=energy,geo`) and incremental updates (`/delta?since=1h` for ~30-50 tokens)
3. **Multi-agent consistency** — shared world context so all agents cite the same probabilities

The data source ([SimpleFunctions](https://simplefunctions.dev/world)) aggregates 9,706 prediction market contracts from Kalshi (CFTC-regulated) and Polymarket into a markdown snapshot optimized for LLM context windows. No API key needed — the endpoint is free and public.

## Motivation

A recurring problem in agent development: LLMs have a knowledge cutoff and don't know what's happening today. Web search returns narratives ("tensions remain elevated"), not data. This cookbook shows a different approach — injecting calibrated probabilities backed by real money into the agent's context.

The prediction market insight: a price of 53c on "Iran invasion" encodes the aggregate judgment of everyone with money at risk on that question. This is fundamentally more useful for agent reasoning than news headlines or search results.

author: chaliy
body:
## Summary

- Emit warning on stderr when sed branch/label loop limit (1000 iterations) is hit
- Warning includes line number for debugging

## What & Why

The sed branch execution loop silently stopped at 1000 iterations, producing silently truncated output. This is a data integrity issue — scripts depending on sed loops would get incorrect results without any indication. Now emits `sed: warning: branch/label loop limit (1000) reached on line N; output may be truncated`.

## Tests Added

- `test_sed_branch_loop_limit_emits_warning` — verifies warning on stderr when limit hit
- `test_sed_normal_branch_no_warning` — verifies no warning for normal sed usage

Closes #1005

author: snissn
body:
## What Changed

- lets fresh segment rewrite planning proceed even when cooled queued debt is present
- preserves cooled queued debt by merging fresh segment plans into the persisted queue/ledger instead of overwriting it
- keeps the current chunk-ledger path intact; this slice only changes fresh segment-plan bypass behavior
- adds scheduler coverage for:
  - cooled debt not blocking a fresh plan
  - fresh ledger merge without overwriting cooled debt
- updates one older ineffective-backoff test to keep asserting queue eligibility instead of accidentally consuming the dedicated queue source

## Why

`#929` through `#932` split queued rewrite into its own source, gated follow-up on reclaim, preferred fresh debt before cooled retries, and capped cooled retries per pass.

The next missing bridge step from the frozen aggressive pivot was allowing fresh work to proceed even when non-executable cooled debt still exists. Without that, cooled debt can still block new segment plans on current `main`.

This port deliberately keeps the change narrow:
- fresh segment plans may bypass cooled debt
- cooled debt is preserved and merged
- fresh chunk-plan bypass is not enabled in this slice

## Impact

- fresh rewrite work can make progress without discarding cooled debt
- queued state remains resumable after the fresh pass
- chunk-ledger semantics on current `main` stay unchanged

## Validation

- `GOWORK=off go test ./TreeDB/caching -run 'Test(VlogGenerationRewriteQueue_(CooledDebtDoesNotBlockFreshPlan|CooledDebtFreshLedgerMergesWithoutOverwrite|PrefersUnpenalizedLedgerBeforeExpiredPenalty|SuppressesImmediateFollowupWithoutUnreferencedBytes|ResumesWithoutReplanning|KeepsStillReferencedSegmentQueuedWhenBounded|ConsumesMissingBoundedSourceIDs|BoundedSegmentEventuallyDrainsWithoutReplanning|DebtDrainProcessesMultipleSegments|LedgerOrdersByStaleRatio)|VlogGenerationMaintenance_(ArmsDedicatedRewriteQueueSourceForExecutableDebt|QueuesPendingCheckpointKickOnActiveCollision)|VlogGenerationRewrite_(QueuedExecIgnoresForegroundCancelUntilBoundedCompletion|IneffectiveBackoffExpires)|VlogGenerationRewritePlan_FiltersPenalizedSegments)$' -count=1`

body:
## Summary

- Patches the test VS Code instance's `product.json` to set `win32VersionedUpdate: false`, bypassing the InnoSetup installer mutex check that causes tests to exit immediately with _"Code is currently being updated"_ when a system VS Code update is in progress
- Adds `gitlens.advanced.skipOnboarding: true` to default test user settings to suppress welcome/onboarding screens that can interfere with E2E tests in ephemeral environments

## Details

On Windows, VS Code checks for a `vscode-updating` mutex created by the InnoSetup installer. If the system VS Code is being updated at the same time tests run, the test VS Code instance sees the mutex and exits with a false-positive error. The patch applies only to the isolated test binary and has no effect on CI (Linux).

The `skipOnboarding` setting prevents unexpected welcome views from appearing in clean test environments.

## Test plan

- [x] `patchTestVSCodeProductJson` is no-op on non-Windows platforms (guarded by `process.platform !== 'win32'`)

author: joeduffy
body:
## Summary

This PR addresses #14501, reported by @typez, who discovered that the `read()` method on dynamic resource providers throws an unimplemented exception rather than actually working — despite the documentation describing it as if it were functional.

## Changes

The dynamic providers documentation (`content/docs/iac/concepts/providers/dynamic-providers.md`) is updated in three places:

1. **Intro paragraph**: Removes `read` from the list of "functions you will probably also want to implement" and adds a note pointing to the `read` section below.

2. **Lifecycle overview**: Adds an inline parenthetical to the lifecycle step that mentions `read`, noting it is not currently implemented.

3. **`### read(id, props)` section**: Adds a prominent `{{% notes type="warning" %}}` block at the top of the section that:
   - Clearly states `read()` is not currently functional
   - Explains what happens when you try to use it (unimplemented exception)
   - References the upstream tracking issue: [pulumi/pulumi#16175](https://github.com/pulumi/pulumi/issues/16175)
   - Suggests using a component resource backed by a native provider if import is needed

The existing description of the `read()` interface contract is preserved but reframed as describing intended behavior ("when `read` is implemented, it is intended to..."), so the docs remain useful as a reference for whenever the feature is eventually implemented. The misleading info note encouraging users to implement `read()` is removed.

Fixes #14501
Tracks upstream: pulumi/pulumi#16175

The `/api/v1/projection/runtime/multi-device` endpoint assembled its projection primarily from raw transport/session registry data. PR-519 added chain and graph snapshots as supplementary metadata only — the projection body remained registry-anchored and could silently present a falsely complete view when canonical result surfacing was incomplete.

## New: `core/multi_device_projection_canonicalization.py` (layer 13)

Canonical enrichment authority that queries all available runtime sources and returns a `MultiDeviceCanonicalEnrichment` with explicit surfacing fidelity:

```python
from core.multi_device_projection_canonicalization import enrich_multi_device_projection

enrichment = enrich_multi_device_projection()
# enrichment.surfacing_state  → FULL | PARTIAL | DEGRADED | UNAVAILABLE
# enrichment.surfacing_gap_reasons  → machine-readable list when sources are missing
# enrichment.transport_local_only   → True only when both chain and graph are absent
```

Sources consumed (all non-fatal): `CrossDeviceChainSingleton`, `TaskGraphRuntime`, `OperatorSurface` (optional), `MultiDeviceControlIntegrityRuntime` (optional).

## Wired into projection endpoint

- Replaces the partial PR-519 inline enrichment block with a single `enrich_multi_device_projection()` call
- Projection metadata now carries `canonical_enrichment`, `canonical_surfacing_state`, `canonical_surfacing_gaps`, `transport_local_only`, and `pr_522_gap_008_resolved`
- Backward-compat keys `cross_device_chain_snapshot` and `task_graph_snapshot` preserved
- `MULTI_DEVICE_PROJECTION_CANONICALIZATION_INTEGRATED` sentinel added to `projection.py`

## Gap catalog

- `GAP-517-008` marked `is_resolved=True` in `multi_device_control_integrity.py`
- `test_pr519` updated: `test_I3` now asserts full resolution by PR-522 (was asserting partial PR-519 note)

## Tests

`tests/test_pr522_multi_device_projection_canonicalization.py` — 82 tests across groups: sentinel imports, enum values, dataclass round-trip, chain/graph/operator/integrity enrichment paths, surfacing state logic (FULL/PARTIAL/UNAVAILABLE), explicit degraded-state gap reasons, endpoint metadata keys, backward-compat keys, gap catalog resolution.

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

# PR-522: Multi-Device Projection Canonicalization

PR-517 identified that the multi-device projection/runtime surface can still derive too much of its state from raw registry/session data instead of consuming the repository’s canonical multi-device execution/runtime state. After PR-519 and PR-520/521 tighten result surfacing, formation truth, and control semantics, the next step is to ensure projection/status views for multi-device state are grounded in canonical chain/runtime truth rather than transport-local approximations.

This PR should improve canonicalization of the multi-device projection surface without turning into a full UI redesign.

## Core goal
Ensure representative multi-device projection/runtime views are enriched from canonical chain/runtime state and not merely from raw transport/session registry data.

## Primary gap to reduce/close
1. **GAP-517-008**
   - The multi-device runtime projection endpoint currently produces a projection based largely on raw registry/session data rather than canonical `CrossDeviceChainSingleton` / `TaskGraphRuntime` state.
   - This can leave the projection inconsistent when cross-device results or formation semantics have only partially surfaced.

## Required outcomes
1. **Enrich projection from canonical multi-device runtime sources**
   - Ensure representative multi-device projection paths consume canonical chain/runtime state where available, such as:
     - cross-device chain execution snapshots,
     - task graph/runtime snapshots,
     - formation/runtime metadata,
     - and related canonical result-surface state.

2. **Reduce raw transport/session authority in projection assembly**
   - Keep transport/session registry data as lower-level supporting input where necessary, but not as the sole or primary authority for final multi-device runtime projection.

3. **Reflect incomplete or degraded canonical surfacing honestly**
   - Where canonical result/formation data is incomplete, projection should expose that degraded/incomplete condition rather than silently presenting a falsely complete view.

4. **Preserve architectural separation**
   - Do not redesign the entire projection UI or status board in this PR.
   - Focus on improving the data authority and enrichment path behind the existing projection/runtime surfaces.

## Non-goals
- Do not perform a full visual redesign or 2.5D/constellation redesign here.
- Do not rewrite unrelated gateway/dispatch logic except where minimal hooks are needed to surface canonical projection data.
- Do not broaden scope into a generic dashboard cleanup.

## Important implementation notes
- Favor projection enrichment from canonical runtime structures over direct registry mirroring.
- Preserve backward-compatible shape where possible, but improve authority ordering and inspection fidelity.
- Make degraded/incomplete canonical state explicit rather than hidden.

## Suggested validation
- Add tests proving representative projection/runtime endpoints include canonical chain/runtime-derived state.
- Add tests proving projection can distinguish complete vs incomplete canonical surfacing.
- Add tests proving raw registry/session data alone is no longer the only authority for representative multi-device runtime projection.
- Update residual integrity docs/tracking to mark projection-related gaps resolved or narrowed.

body:
## Description

Multiple code paths used `resolve_config(profile)` which only loads global + profile config, silently dropping repo-level overrides from `.agent-of-empires/config.toml`. This caused settings like `bare_repo_path_template`, `delete_branch_on_cleanup`, and `auto_cleanup` to be ignored when set at the repo level.

The reported bug (#568) was that `aoe add --worktree` ignores repo-level `bare_repo_path_template`, but the same pattern existed in three other places:

- **`src/cli/add.rs`** -- the reported bug. Worktree path template resolution now uses `resolve_config_with_repo`.
- **`src/cli/remove.rs`** -- `delete_branch_on_cleanup` and `sandbox.auto_cleanup` from repo config were ignored during session removal.
- **`src/tui/dialogs/delete_options.rs`** -- delete dialog defaults (auto_cleanup checkboxes) ignored repo config. Added `project_path` to `DeleteDialogConfig` to enable repo-aware config resolution.
- **`src/tui/dialogs/new_session/mod.rs`** -- new session dialog defaults (default_tool, sandbox settings) ignored repo config from cwd.

Two callsites were intentionally **not** changed:
- `src/tui/home/input.rs:1179` (`resolve_global_profile_hooks_for`) -- function explicitly scoped to global+profile hooks only
- `src/tui/home/mod.rs:895` (`refresh_from_config`) -- refreshes global TUI state, not project-specific

author: copilot
body: Thanks for asking me to work on this. I will get started on it and keep this PR's description up to date as I form a plan and make progress. > ---- > > *This section details on the original issue you should resolve* > > feat: Advanced DSP Upgrades — adaptive Wiener filter, DNS v2 ONNX model, multi-speaker separation, harmonic enhancer v2 > # Advanced DSP Capability Upgrades > > ## Goal > Extend the existing 32-stage DSP pipeline (`dsp-core.js`) with improved noise suppression, a production-grade deep learning model, multi-speaker source separation, and an upgraded harmonic enhancer. Nothing removed — all additions layered on top of the existing pipeline. > > ## Current DSP State (from dsp-core.js) > - Pass 1: DC removal, peak normalization > - Pass 2: Noise gate, notch filters, click removal, de-essing, de-reverberation > - Pass 5: Wiener-MMSE spectral subtraction, 32 ERB band gate, harmonic enhancement, temporal smoothing, late reverb subtraction > - Pass 7: Parametric EQ > - Pass 8: Downward expander + compressor > - Pass 9: Stereo widening, true peak limiter, TPDF dithering > - ML: Silero VAD, DeepFilterNet3, Demucs v4 > > ## Required Enhancements > > ### 1. Adaptive Wiener Filter (upgrade Pass 5) > Current implementation uses a fixed noise floor estimate. Upgrade to a **per-bin adaptive noise floor** that: > - Tracks noise floor independently per FFT bin using a minimum statistics tracker (Martin 2001 algorithm) > - Updates noise estimate only during VAD-inactive frames (silence / non-speech) > - Applies a speech presence probability weighting (SPP) to avoid over-suppression during speech > - Smoothing time constant: configurable (default 200ms) > > ```js > // Target API (no breaking changes) > applyAdaptiveWiener(fftBins, vad, noiseFloorTracker, { smoothingMs: 200, overSubtraction: 1.2 }) > ``` > > ### 2. DNS v2 ONNX Model (upgrade ml-worker.js) > Replace or supplement DeepFilterNet3 with **Microsoft DNS Challenge v2 model** (ONNX format): > - Model: `dns2_conformer_small.onnx` (~8MB, runs in ONNX Runtime Web) > - Input: 512-point STFT magnitude frames, 16kHz sample rate > - Output: gain mask per frequency bin (0..1) > - Apply gain mask multiplicatively after Wiener filter (Pass 5) > - Fallback: if ONNX model fails to load, continue with Wiener-only path (no crash) > - Worker message: `{ type: 'dns2_mask', mask: Float32Array }` > > ### 3. Multi-Speaker Source Separation (new Pass 4.5) > Insert a new pass between Pass 4 and Pass 5 using **Conv-TasNet** or **SepFormer** (lightweight ONNX variant): > - Input: mixed audio frame (time domain) > - Output: up to 4 separated source streams > - Each stream tagged with speaker ID from fingerprinting module (issue Joker5514/VoiceIsolate-Pro#251) > - Only the target speaker stream proceeds to Pass 5; others are attenuated (not discarded — kept at -24dB for monitoring) > - Configurable: `separationMode: 'target-only' | 'all-speakers' | 'off'` > > ### 4. Harmonic Enhancer v2 (upgrade Pass 5) > Current harmonic enhancement uses pitch-tracked boost. Upgrade to: > - **Spectral band replication (SBR)**: synthesize harmonics above 8kHz from lower-band content > - **Formant preservation**: detect F1/F2 formants via LPC analysis, protect them from over-suppression > - **Breathiness control**: separate aperiodic (breathy) component from periodic (voiced) component, allow independent gain control > - Configurable via preset: `{ sbr: true, formantProtection: true, breathinessGain: 0.8 }` > > ### 5. Real-Time Noise Classification > Add a lightweight classifier that identifies the noise type and adjusts suppression strategy: > - Classes: `music`, `white_noise`, `crowd`, `HVAC`, `keyboard`, `traffic`, `silence` > - Model: small CNN (< 500KB ONNX) running in `ml-worker.js` > - Output: `{ noiseClass: string, confidence: number }` — emitted to UI for display > - Strategy map: > - `music` → increase Wiener over-subtraction, enable Demucs vocal stem extraction > - `white_noise` → standard Wiener > - `crowd` → enable multi-speaker separation > - `HVAC` / `traffic` → adaptive noise floor with fast tracking > > ### 6. Latency Budget > All new passes must fit within the existing latency budget: > - Target: < 40ms total pipeline latency at 48kHz, 512-sample hop > - DNS v2 inference: < 8ms per frame (ONNX Runtime Web, WASM backend) > - Noise classifier: < 3ms per frame > - Source separation: < 15ms per frame (only when enabled) > > ## Files to Modify > - `dsp-core.js` — adaptive Wiener, harmonic enhancer v2, noise classifier integration > - `ml-worker.js` — DNS v2 ONNX model, noise classifier model, source separation model > - `pipeline-orchestrator.js` — insert Pass 4.5, wire up new model outputs > - `pipeline-state.js` — add state fields for noise class, separation mode, adaptive noise floor > > ## Acceptance Criteria > - [ ] Adaptive Wiener filter tracks noise floor per-bin, updates only during silence > - [ ] DNS v2 ONNX model loads and applies gain mask; graceful fallback if load fails > - [ ] Multi-speaker separation produces up to 4 streams; target stream routed to Pass 5 > - [ ] Harmonic enhancer v2 preserves formants and adds SBR above 8kHz > - [ ] Noise classifier emits correct class with >80% accuracy on test set > - [ ] Total pipeline latency remains < 40ms at 48kHz/512-hop > - [ ] No regression in existing audio output quality > - [ ] All new passes are individually toggleable via config flags > > > ## Comments on the Issue (you are @copilot in this section) > > > ---

body:
## Description

Adds the missing `user_migration_approve.schema.json` schema file and registers `user_migration_approve` in `getNotificationTypes()`.

The `crm-integration-consumer` was crashing on every `USER_MIGRATION_APPROVE` message with:
> `invalid payload type user_migration_approve`

The error originates in `pkg/validator/validate.go` — the validator lowercases the message type and looks it up in a `schemasMap`. Since neither the schema file nor the type registration ever existed, every message failed validation before reaching the handler.

The schema mirrors the existing `user_migration` schema but without `migration_reference` (which is not part of the approve payload), matching the `UserMigrationApproveRequest` struct in `crm-integration-api`.

body:
**Version Bump:** Removing the exported methods `(*ClientFacingActivity).GetWheelchairUse()` and `(*ClientFacingProfile).GetWheelchairUse()` is a breaking change — existing callers will fail to compile.

- The `GetWheelchairUse()` accessor method has been removed from both `ClientFacingActivity` and `ClientFacingProfile`. Callers that reference these methods must be updated — remove calls to `GetWheelchairUse()` or access the `WheelchairUse` field directly on the struct instead.
- The SDK now supports three new query expression types: `DerivedReadinessColumnExpr` for readiness-related columns (chronotype, sleep score, recovery score, recovery zone, stress score, strain score, strain zone), `InsulinInjectionTimeseriesExpr` for insulin injection timeseries data (replacing the former `IntervalTimeseriesExprTimeseriesInsulinInjection` constant), and `AwakeningsValueMacroExpr` for awakenings macro expressions. All three are available as variants in `AggregateExprArg`, `QueryGroupByItem`, and `QuerySelectItem`.

**Breaking changes:** The `AggregateExprArgVisitor`, `QueryGroupByItemVisitor`, and `QuerySelectItemVisitor` interfaces each gain three new required `Visit*` methods (`VisitDerivedReadinessColumnExpr`, `VisitAwakeningsValueMacroExpr`, `VisitInsulinInjectionTimeseriesExpr`) — any existing implementations must add these methods. The `IntervalTimeseriesExprTimeseriesInsulinInjection` constant has been removed. The `Placeholder` struct's `Placeholder` field is now a private literal (accessed via the `Placeholder()` method); the exported `GetPlaceholder()` and `SetPlaceholder()` methods have been removed. `QueryBatch.Timeframe` and `QueryBatch.Queries` JSON tags no longer use `omitempty`.
- **Breaking changes** to `ParsingJob` and `ResultMetadata`:

- `ParsingJob.JobId` field and its `GetJobId`/`SetJobId` methods have been removed. The new `FailureReason` field (type `ParsingJobFailureReason`) is available in its place, along with a new `ParsingJobFailureReason` enum (`invalid_input`, `low_quality`, `not_english`).
- `ResultMetadata` fields `PatientFirstName`, `PatientLastName`, `Dob`, and `LabName` are now `*string` (previously `string`); callers must dereference these values and update calls to their corresponding `Set*` methods to pass pointer arguments.
- `BodyCreateLabReportParserJob.File` changed from `io.Reader` to `[]io.Reader`; wrap existing single-reader usages in a slice.
- A new `Gender` field (`*ResultMetadataGender`) has been added to `ResultMetadata`, along with a new `ResultMetadataGender` enum (`male`, `female`, `other`).
- Several breaking changes have been made to bulk-operation request types. The `TeamId` field and `SetTeamId` method have been removed from `BulkExportConnectionsBody`, `BulkImportConnectionsBody`, `BulkPauseConnectionsBody`, `BulkTriggerHistoricalPullBody`, and `LinkListBulkOpsRequest`; callers referencing these fields must remove them. The exported types `LinkBulkExportRequestTeamId`, `LinkBulkImportRequestTeamId`, `LinkBulkPauseRequestTeamId`, `LinkBulkTriggerHistoricalPullRequestTeamId`, and `LinkListBulkOpsRequestTeamId` have also been removed. Additionally, `ClientFacingSleep` now includes a new `RecoveryReadinessScore` field, `ManualConnectionData` gains `VitalIosSdkVersion`, `VitalAndroidSdkVersion`, and `GrantedPermissions` fields, and new enum values `ManualProvidersSamsungHealth` and `PasswordProvidersTandemSource` are available.
- The SDK now includes a wide set of new types and fields for lab ordering, order tracking, and lab result parsing.

**New types and events:**
- `BiomarkerResult`, `MissingBiomarkerResult`, and `ParentBiomarkerData` for structured lab result data.
- `ClientFacingLabReportParsingJobCreatedEvent` and `ClientFacingLabReportParsingJobUpdatedEvent` webhook events for lab report parsing jobs.
- `ClientFacingOrderTransaction` and `ClientFacingOrderInTransaction` for order transaction tracking.
- `LabResultsRaw`, `LabResultsMetadata`, `SampleData`, `PerformingLaboratory`, and `ClinicalInformation` for raw lab result payloads.
- `UtcTimestampWithTimezoneOffset` for timezone-aware timestamps in lab result sample data.

**New fields:**
- `ClientFacingOrder` now includes `last_event`, `clinical_notes`, `origin`, and `order_transaction`.
- `ClientFacingOrderEvent` now includes `status_detail`.
- `Address`, `PatientAddressCompatible`, and `PatientAddressWithValidation` now include `access_notes`.

**New enum values:**
- `OrderLowLevelStatus`, `OrderOrigin`, `OrderStatusDetail`, and `OrderTransactionStatus` enums added.
- New corrected order status constants (e.g., `completed.testkit.corrected`).
- Additional `Labs`, `Providers`, and `PayorCodeExternalProvider` values.
- Several breaking changes are included in this release:

- `UserInfo.GetAddress()` and `UserInfo.SetAddress()` (and the same methods on `UserInfoCreateRequest`) now use `*UserAddress` instead of `*Address`. Update any code that passes or receives an `*Address` to use `*UserAddress`.
- `UserRefreshSuccessResponse` no longer exposes the `Success` field, `GetSuccess()`, or `SetSuccess()`. The `success` JSON literal is now validated internally; use the new `Success() bool` method to read it.
- `BookPscAppointment` on both `labtests.Client` and `labtests.RawClient` now accepts `*vitalgo.LabTestsBookPscAppointmentRequest` instead of `*vitalgo.AppointmentBookingRequest`.
- `labreport.ParserCreateJob` now expects `request.File` to be a slice rather than a single file.
- Bulk link operations (`BulkImport`, `BulkTriggerHistoricalPull`, `BulkExport`, `BulkPause`) no longer append query parameters from the request struct.

New additions include `Compendium`, `LabAccount`, and `OrderTransaction` sub-clients on the root `Client`, new insulin delivery enum types (`DeliveryMode`, `DeliveryForm`, `BolusPurpose`) on `ClientFacingInsulinInjectionSample`, and a new `ClientFacingDeviceSourceTypeInsulinPump` enum value.
- The SDK now includes types for lab test compendium search and conversion. New types include `SearchCompendiumBody`, `ConvertCompendiumBody`, `SearchCompendiumResponse`, `ConvertCompendiumResponse`, `CanonicalCandidate`, `PerLabCandidate`, `RelatedCandidate`, and `ProviderIdConversionResponse`, along with the `CompendiumSearchLabs` and `SearchMode` enums.
- The SDK now includes two new API client packages: `compendium` (with `Search` and `Convert` methods for lab test data) and `labaccount` (with `GetTeamLabAccounts` for managing team lab accounts). New types `ClientFacingLabAccount`, `GetTeamLabAccountsResponse`, `LabAccountDelegatedFlow`, `LabAccountStatus`, and `UsState` are also available. The `insulin_pump` source type has been added to the electrocardiogram and menstrual cycle source type enums.
- The SDK now includes a new `ordertransaction` package providing `GetTransaction`, `GetTransactionResult`, and `GetTransactionResultPdf` methods for accessing order transaction data and lab results via the `/v3/order_transaction` endpoints. New exported types `GetOrderTransactionResponse` and `OrderSummary` are available in the top-level package. A new `insulin_pump` source type constant (`ClientFacingSleepCycleSourceTypeInsulinPump`) has also been added to the sleep cycle source type enum.

## Summary

- New `@script-development/fs-translation` package — type-safe reactive i18n service for Vue 3
- Multi-locale with runtime switching via reactive `locale` ref
- Dot-notation keys (`"section.name"`) with compile-time validation via `NestedKeys<TSchema>`
- Parameter interpolation via `{param}` placeholders
- Memoized computed refs — same key+params returns same `ComputedRef` instance
- Dependency: `string-ts` (for `replaceAll`). Peer dep: Vue 3.5+

## Package API

```ts
const { t, locale } = createTranslationService({
  en: { common: { save: "Save" }, errors: { required: "{field} is required" } },
  nl: { common: { save: "Opslaan" }, errors: { required: "{field} is verplicht" } },
}, "en");

t("common.save").value              // "Save"
t("errors.required", { field: "Name" }).value  // "Name is required"
locale.value = "nl";
t("common.save").value              // "Opslaan" (reactive)
```

body: What was broken The earlier PM-4627 fix restored saved iterative reviewers only when the resource role was named `Iterative Reviewer` or `Iterative Review`. Some F2F drafts still reopened with missing reviewer member ids or hit task-only launch validation even though the challenge used the manual reviewers flow. Root cause Iterative-review resources can also be stored under the generic `Reviewer` role, so HumanReviewTab still failed to map those saved assignments back into the reviewer rows after save/reset. ChallengeEditorForm also inferred task mode from a legacy root `reviewer` value even when manual reviewer rows were already present on an F2F draft. What was changed HumanReviewTab now treats `Reviewer` as a fallback iterative-review role alias so saved F2F reviewer assignments repopulate from generic reviewer resources.
