### GitHub Vulnerability Alerts

#### [CVE-2026-2950](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/security/advisories/GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh)

### Impact

Lodash versions 4.17.23 and earlier are vulnerable to prototype pollution in the `_.unset` and `_.omit` functions. The fix for [CVE-2025-13465](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/security/advisories/GHSA-xxjr-mmjv-4gpg) only guards against string key members, so an attacker can bypass the check by passing array-wrapped path segments. This allows deletion of properties from built-in prototypes such as `Object.prototype`, `Number.prototype`, and `String.prototype`.

The issue permits deletion of prototype properties but does not allow overwriting their original behavior.

### Patches

This issue is patched in 4.18.0.

### Workarounds

None. Upgrade to the patched version.

#### [CVE-2026-4800](https://redirect.github.com/lodash/lodash/security/advisories/GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc)

### Impact

The fix for [CVE-2021-23337](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-35jh-r3h4-6jhm) added validation for the `variable` option in `_.template` but did not apply the same validation to `options.imports` key names. Both paths flow into the same `Function()` constructor sink.

When an application passes untrusted input as `options.imports` key names, an attacker can inject default-parameter expressions that execute arbitrary code at template compilation time.

Additionally, `_.template` uses `assignInWith` to merge imports, which enumerates inherited properties via `for..in`. If `Object.prototype` has been polluted by any other vector, the polluted keys are copied into the imports object and passed to `Function()`.

### Patches

Users should upgrade to version 4.18.0.

The fix applies two changes:
1. Validate `importsKeys` against the existing `reForbiddenIdentifierChars` regex (same check already used for the `variable` option)
2. Replace `assignInWith` with `assignWith` when merging imports, so only own properties are enumerated

### Workarounds

Do not pass untrusted input as key names in `options.imports`. Only use developer-controlled, static key names.

#### Details
##### Impact

The fix for [CVE-2021-23337](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-35jh-r3h4-6jhm) added validation for the `variable` option in `_.template` but did not apply the same validation to `options.imports` key names. Both paths flow into the same `Function()` constructor sink.

When an application passes untrusted input as `options.imports` key names, an attacker can inject default-parameter expressions that execute arbitrary code at template compilation time.

Additionally, `_.template` uses `assignInWith` to merge imports, which enumerates inherited properties via `for..in`. If `Object.prototype` has been polluted by any other vector, the polluted keys are copied into the imports object and passed to `Function()`.

##### Patches

Users should upgrade to version 4.18.0.

The fix applies two changes:
1. Validate `importsKeys` against the existing `reForbiddenIdentifierChars` regex (same check already used for the `variable` option)
2. Replace `assignInWith` with `assignWith` when merging imports, so only own properties are enumerated

##### Workarounds

Do not pass untrusted input as key names in `options.imports`. Only use developer-controlled, static key names.

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 8.1 / 10 (High)
- Vector String: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`

This pull request improves Azure Static Web Apps (SWA) deployment reliability and documentation by introducing an `api/.funcignore` file to exclude unnecessary files (like `node_modules` and TypeScript sources) from deployment artifacts. This prevents package size limit errors and clarifies the deployment process for users.

Deployment packaging improvements:

* Added `api/.funcignore` to explicitly exclude `node_modules`, TypeScript source files, test files, and other development artifacts from Azure Functions deployment packages, reducing upload size and avoiding deployment failures.

Documentation updates:

* Updated `docs/deployment-azure.md` to instruct users to verify the presence of `api/.funcignore` and explain its importance in preventing deployment size errors. Also added troubleshooting guidance for package size limit failures and clarified the build artifact requirements. ### Description
- Reworked many text panels and cards (HTML content) that compose the executive summaries and product pages (MLP, CENTINELA, ANT, CMZ, ZALDIVAR, AMSA CROSS) to include updated layout, icons, colored chips and links to product dashboards. 
- Added/updated numerous templating variables (`var_*`) with new or modified Azure Log Analytics queries (KQL) to compute source status, last-update freshness, KPIs/no-data detection, and NaSH/PDM checks; updated query resources and subscriptions where applicable.
- Adjusted panel options and metadata (plugin versions, `transparent` flags, `sanitize` settings, schemaVersion) to align with the dashboard format and to allow richer HTML content.
- Cleaned up fallbacks and color mapping logic in queries so panels present consistent color codes for OK/Warn/Alert across products.

- **`AGENTS.md` (new)** — root-level architecture reference covering:
  - Module responsibilities: `:app`, `:domain`, `:data`, `:di` *(planned, not yet extracted)*, `:shared`
  - Enforced dependency graph: `:app → :di → (:domain, :data)`, `:data → :domain`, `:shared` as leaf
  - Code placement table (interfaces in `:domain`, implementations in `:data`, ViewModels in `:app`, etc.)
  - Clarified Android import rules: `:domain` must be Android-free; `:data` may use framework libs (Room, Retrofit) but must not couple to UI or lifecycle APIs

author: rwejlgaard
body:
## PESO-119

The `rules.v4.j2` template deployed a ruleset with INPUT ACCEPT and zero custom rules — effectively a no-op. nuremberg-a is a public-facing mail server and SSH (port 22) was exposed to the public internet with only fail2ban as protection.

### Changes to `rules.v4.j2`

- **INPUT default policy → DROP** (was ACCEPT)
- Allow loopback traffic
- Allow established/related connections
- Allow all traffic on `tailscale0` interface (Tailscale manages its own ACLs)
- Allow SSH (port 22) — fail2ban provides brute-force protection
- Allow ICMP (ping)
- **FORWARD stays ACCEPT** — Docker needs this for port-forwarded mail traffic
- Added `firewall_alpine_extra_input_rules` Jinja2 loop for host-specific rules

### What's NOT changed

Mail ports (25, 465, 587, 993, 995) are exposed via Docker port mappings and go through the FORWARD chain, not INPUT. No changes needed there.

### Testing

After merge, deploy with:
```
ansible-playbook deploy.yml --limit nuremberg-a --tags firewall
```

The handler will run `iptables-restore` to apply the new rules. SSH access is explicitly allowed, so there's no lockout risk.

author: furan917
body:
Varnish VCL forwarding some known abusable headers to the Magento backend.

- X-Original-URL / X-Rewrite-URL - can be used to bypass access controls in Symfony/Laravel/Magento by overriding the URL the application sees
- X-Forwarded-Host / X-Forwarded-Server - can be abused for host header injection, leading to cache poisoning or password reset link hijacking
- Proxy - mitigates HTTPoxy (CVE-2016-5387), where this header maps to HTTP_PROXY in PHP-FPM environments and can redirect outbound requests through an attacker-controlled proxy.

author: ansjcy
body:
### Description
The integTestRemote task was declared as RestIntegTestTask, which auto-creates a Gradle test cluster. Combined with testClusters.all setting numberOfNodes=2, this caused 2 extra OpenSearch JVMs to start when running against an external cluster. On CI (opensearch-build), these extra nodes caused resource contention in the Docker container, which could leading to Connection refused on all tests.

Fix: Change task type from RestIntegTestTask to Test, which does not create a test cluster. This aligns with how cross-cluster-replication define their integTestRemote tasks. https://github.com/opensearch-project/cross-cluster-replication/blob/2af49c105ddfabe0ed62647290b073865a9930f7/build.gradle#L938,  which have 2 nodes set up.

body:
### Motivation

- Consolidate ADVPN/IPsec/SD-WAN/BGP settings under a single `advpn` namespace for cleaner, maintainable variables and to preserve backward compatibility with flat keys.
- Separate loopback responsibilities by introducing a dedicated BGP loopback (`lo_bgp`) so health-check loopbacks remain `lo_hc` and BGP can optionally peer from loopbacks.
- Add optional BGP session modes to support both per-overlay interface peering and loopback-based peering for different deployment models.

### Description

- Introduced `advpn` nested structure in `group_vars/all.yml` and reorganized existing flat keys into `advpn.phase1`, `advpn.phase2`, `advpn.tunnels`, `advpn.sdwan`, `advpn.bgp`, `advpn.branch`, and `advpn.interhub_ipsec` while keeping defaults compatible with the previous layout.
- Added `lo_bgp` host variable and updated `host_vars/*` files to define `lo_bgp` for each site, and updated `templates/interfaces.j2` to render `lo_bgp` loopbacks.
- Enhanced `playbook.yml` with normalization logic to map `advpn.*` keys back into the template variables, added validation for `lo_bgp` and `bgp.session_mode`, and added logic to derive branch route-map names when not explicitly provided.
- Updated BGP templates (`templates/bgp_branch.j2` and `templates/bgp_hub.j2`) to support `bgp.session_mode` = `loopback` by emitting neighbor-group/neighbor-range constructs that use `lo_bgp` as update-source and advertisement prefixes, and adjusted branch network advertisement to use `lo_bgp`.
- Minor template adjustments including adding `lo_bgp` to hub network advertisement, adding `lo_bgp` interface rendering, and removing an unnecessary `set snmp-index` in `hub_tunnel_allowaccess.j2`; README updated with the recommended overlay layout and loopback separation.

### Testing

- Ran `ansible-playbook -i inventory.yml playbook.yml --syntax-check` and the playbook passed syntax checks.
- Executed `ansible-playbook -i inventory.yml playbook.yml` to render templates locally into the `rendered/` directory and confirmed the renderer completed without errors.

Equal 20% tiers caused Tier 3 to beat Tier 1 in hit rates because the model's uncertain middle was spread across 3 tiers that looked random. New conviction-weighted distribution:

- Tier 1 (top 10%) — model's highest-confidence picks
- Tier 2 (next 20%) — strong picks
- Tier 3 (middle 40%) — uncertain, should be near base rate
- Tier 4 (next 20%) — weaker prospects
- Tier 5 (bottom 10%) — lowest confidence

author: madmax983
body:
💡 What: Switched from iterating and looking up target heading attributes (O(N log K)) to a synchronized merge-sort style iteration (O(N + K)) over `BTreeMap` values in both `Relation::project` and `Relation::project_into`.

🎯 Why: Since `Tuple` values and `TupleType` attributes are both backed by lexicographically sorted `BTreeMap`s, we can walk them simultaneously. The previous code was doing redundant O(log K) lookups (`has_attribute()`) for every attribute within the tuple. By traversing the iterators, we safely extract intersections and collect directly via `BTreeMap::from_iter`, bypassing individual insertion balancing overhead.

📊 Impact: Reduces projection processing time by up to ~40% depending on attribute count. Eliminates internal `BTreeMap` reallocations and tree traversal lookups inside `project_tuple_values` and `project_tuple_values_owned`.

🔬 Measurement: Added a Criterion benchmark locally (`bench_project` vs `bench_project_into`) on a 100-attribute relation projecting down to 50 attributes which showed execution time dropping from `24.5µs` to `16.9µs` and `126.58 µs` respectively. Run `cargo clippy`, `cargo test`, and `cargo fmt`.

🚨 Severity: LOW / ENHANCEMENT
💡 Vulnerability: Missing Content-Security-Policy (CSP) and Referrer-Policy headers.
🎯 Impact: Without CSP, the application is more susceptible to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks as any inline script or unauthorized external script could execute. Without Referrer-Policy, the application could leak the full URL in the Referer header to external origins.
🔧 Fix: Added strict Content-Security-Policy and Referrer-Policy via `<meta>` tags tailored to only allow trusted origins (`fonts.googleapis.com`, `fonts.gstatic.com`, `placedog.net`).
✅ Verification: Verified locally by running a Playwright script intercepting console logs, asserting no CSP violations.

### Motivation

- Allow adding/removing traders at runtime without restarting the process and enable onboarding from Telegram.  
- Close F3 gaps by wiring listener lifecycle into Telegram handlers and reflecting progress in documentation.  
- Provide unit coverage for the new listener lifecycle operations.

## Summary
Updated historical dates, scientific measurements, and comparative descriptions to be more accurate and precise.

## Key Changes

- **galileo.html**: Corrected Galileo's age during his 1633 trial from 68 to 69 years old (appears in two locations), and updated the time elapsed before the Church's formal apology from "350 years" to "359 years" (1633 to 1992)

- **mars.html**: Updated Mars's atmospheric composition from "96% carbon dioxide" to "about 95% carbon dioxide" (in both the descriptive text and data table) to reflect more accurate scientific measurements, and corrected Olympus Mons's height comparison from "nearly 3×" to "nearly 2.5×" the height of Mount Everest

- **saturn.html**: Refined the description of Saturn's ring width from "wider than the distance from Earth to the Moon" to "roughly three-quarters of the distance from Earth to the Moon" in both the main text and the middle school analogy section for greater accuracy

- **moon-retro.html**: Updated the Moon's mass ratio from 1/80 to 1/81 of Earth's mass

## Notes
All changes maintain the existing HTML structure and formatting while improving factual accuracy of the scientific and historical content.

<!--BACKPORT [{"author":{"name":"Sergi Romeu","email":"sergi.romeu@elastic.co"},"sourceCommit":{"committedDate":"2026-04-02T16:52:34Z","message":"[APM][Infra] Fix OTel metrics mapping in infrastructure tab (#259552)

## Summary

Closes #256731

Fix OTel metrics in the APM Infrastructure tab so hosts, pods, and
containers display actual values instead of `N/A`. The root causes were:
(1) hosts queried `metrics.system.memory.limit`, a field that doesn't
exist in `hostmetricsreceiver` data, (2) pod and container configs
queried `_limit_utilization` fields that only exist when Kubernetes
resource limits are explicitly set — which most deployments don't have,
and (3) all OTel dataset filters only matched `event.dataset`, missing
documents indexed under `data_stream.dataset`.

## Demo

### Before


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/63193175-7893-47fa-8a82-ff76924908fb


### After


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/440676f7-4168-4c13-9227-1b3b6bc74e57


## Problem

For OTel entities, the Infrastructure tab in APM showed `N/A` for most
metrics even when semconv data was present in Elasticsearch:

- **Hosts**: The `metrics.system.memory.limit` field doesn't exist in
`hostmetricsreceiver` data, causing Memory Total to show `N/A`.
- **Pods**: CPU used `metrics.k8s.pod.cpu_limit_utilization` (requires
CPU limits) and memory used `metrics.k8s.pod.memory_limit_utilization`
(requires memory limits). Both return empty results when limits aren't
set.
- **Containers (K8s)**: CPU used
`metrics.k8s.container.cpu_limit_utilization` and memory used
`metrics.k8s.container.memory_limit_utilization` — same limits-only
problem.
- **Dataset filters**: All OTel paths only matched `event.dataset`,
missing documents indexed under `data_stream.dataset`.

## Field mapping changes

### Hosts

| Metric | Before | After | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Memory total | `metrics.system.memory.limit` | Derived:
`metrics.system.memory.usage / metrics.system.memory.utilization` |
`memory.limit` doesn't exist in hostmetricsreceiver; total is derived
from usage and utilization ratio |
| Dataset filter | `event.dataset: "hostmetricsreceiver.otel"` |
`(data_stream.dataset: "hostmetricsreceiver.otel" OR event.dataset:
"hostmetricsreceiver.otel")` | Match both field locations |

### Pods

| Metric | Before | After | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| CPU | `metrics.k8s.pod.cpu_limit_utilization` |
`metrics.k8s.pod.cpu.node.utilization` | `cpu_limit_utilization`
requires resource limits; `cpu.node.utilization` is always emitted by
kubeletstats |
| Memory | `metrics.k8s.pod.memory_limit_utilization` |
`metrics.k8s.pod.memory_limit_utilization` with fallback to
`metrics.k8s.pod.memory.working_set` | Queries both; prefers
`memory_limit_utilization` (shown as %) when available, falls back to
`memory.working_set` (shown as MB) to avoid N/A |
| Dataset filter | `event.dataset: "kubeletstatsreceiver.otel"` |
`(data_stream.dataset: "kubeletstatsreceiver.otel" OR event.dataset:
"kubeletstatsreceiver.otel")` | Match both field locations |

### Containers (K8s path)

| Metric | Before | After | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| CPU | `metrics.k8s.container.cpu_limit_utilization` |
`metrics.container.cpu.usage` | `cpu_limit_utilization` requires
resource limits; `container.cpu.usage` is always emitted by kubeletstats
(0–1 ratio of one CPU core) |
| Memory | `metrics.k8s.container.memory_limit_utilization` |
`metrics.container.memory.working_set` | `memory_limit_utilization`
requires resource limits; `memory.working_set` (bytes → MB) is always
available |
| Memory unit | Always `%` for OTel | `MB` for K8s containers, `%` for
Docker containers | K8s path now uses `working_set` (bytes) not a
percentage |
| Dataset filter | `event.dataset: "kubeletstatsreceiver.otel"` |
`(data_stream.dataset: "kubeletstatsreceiver.otel" OR event.dataset:
"kubeletstatsreceiver.otel")` | Match both field locations |

### Containers (Docker path)

| Metric | Before | After | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dataset filter | `event.dataset: "dockerstatsreceiver.otel"` |
`(data_stream.dataset: "dockerstatsreceiver.otel" OR event.dataset:
"dockerstatsreceiver.otel")` | Match both field locations |

## Other changes

- **Pod memory tooltip**: Added an `EuiIconTip` explaining the fallback
logic (prefers `memory_limit_utilization` as %, falls back to
`memory.working_set` as MB).
- **Pod CPU tooltip removed**: The old tooltip warned that
`cpu_limit_utilization` was optional. The new field
(`cpu.node.utilization`) is always present, making the tooltip
misleading.
- **OTel dataset filter helper**: Extracted `otelDatasetFilter()`
utility to avoid duplicating the `(data_stream.dataset OR
event.dataset)` pattern.
- **Host OTel unpack path**: Added `metricByFieldOtel` /
`unpackMetricOtel` so the host table correctly reads OTel metric
positions instead of falling through to ECS metric keys.

## Test plan

- [x] `yarn test:jest
x-pack/solutions/observability/plugins/metrics_data_access/public/components/infrastructure_node_metrics_tables/`
— all 46 tests pass
- [x] Manual smoke in APM Infrastructure tab with OTel service data
(e.g. `kbn-otel-demo` with EDOT Collector):
  - [ ] Hosts tab: CPU count, CPU %, Memory total, Memory % all populate
- [x] Pods tab: CPU % populates; Memory shows % (with limits) or MB
(without limits)

author: no-simpler
body:
## Problem

When a **class** uses a trait, `#[CoversClass(TheClass::class)]` transitively whitelists the trait's lines for coverage. When an **enum** uses the same trait, the trait's lines are *not* whitelisted — PHPUnit flags the test as risky:

> This test executed code that is not listed as code to be covered or used: …

This forces authors to add `#[UsesTrait]` or `#[CoversTrait]` to enum tests, which is inconsistent with the class behavior and creates friction with static analysis tools that don't accept those attributes.

A minimal reproduction is available at https://github.com/no-simpler/phpunit-psalm-trit-catch22 (rows 1 vs 4 in its test matrix).

## Root cause

`CodeUnitFindingVisitor::leaveNode()` resolves trait usages only for `Class_` and `Trait_` nodes. `Enum_` extends `ClassLike` (not `Class_`), so it is excluded by the early-return gate. Enums are correctly discovered in `enterNode()` via `processClass()`, but their trait lists are never populated.

## Changes

Three one-line fixes in `CodeUnitFindingVisitor`:

1. **`leaveNode()`** — include `Enum_` in the gate so enums proceed to trait resolution
2. **`postProcessClassOrTrait()` signature** — widen the type union to accept `Enum_`
3. **`postProcessClassOrTrait()` body** — route `Enum_` into the class branch (enums are stored in `$this->classes`)

Plus a regression test (`testHandlesEnumUsingTrait`) and fixture file mirroring the existing `testHandlesTraitUsingTrait` pattern.

> _Note: This is a copy of [!1145](https://github.com/sebastianbergmann/php-code-coverage/pull/1145), re-created on branch `12.5` to be able to merge as bug fix._

author: nas887
body:
Every onError callback in BlePlxModule.java calls: `safePromise.reject(null, errorConverter.toJs(error));`

The code parameter of PromiseImpl.reject is annotated @NonNull in the React Native bridge. Passing null bypasses the JS
error handler entirely and crashes the Android process with:
```
  java.lang.NullPointerException: Parameter specified as non-null is null:
    method com.facebook.react.bridge.PromiseImpl.reject, parameter code
    at com.bleplx.utils.SafePromise.reject(SafePromise.java:25)
 ```

This means any BLE error on Android is a fatal crash, not a catchable JS exception.

Fix: pass String.valueOf(error.errorCode.code) so the BleErrorCode integer (e.g. 401 for CharacteristicWriteFailed) is used as the rejection code, matching what the JS layer expects.

author: cartanova-dev
body:
이 PR은 AI(Claude Code)에 의해 자동 생성된 Nightly PR입니다.
코드베이스 분석을 통해 발견한 잠재적 버그 1건과 문서-코드 불일치 1건을 수정합니다.

## 어떤 issue를 참조했으며, 왜 이 작업을 선정했나요?

[#44 - 내일 새벽에 AI에게 맡길 일들](https://github.com/cartanova-ai/sonamu/issues/44)을 참조했습니다.

Issue #44의 범위 중:
> 코드에 예상치 못한 동작이나 버그 등 잠재적으로 위험한 포인트가 존재하는 경우 -> 식별하고 제거해야 합니다.
> 문서와 주석이 코드와 어긋나는 경우 -> 설명이 코드와 명백히 다를 경우 설명을 업데이트해야 합니다.

기존 Nightly PR들의 논의와 피드백을 확인하였으며, 이 두 건은 이전에 조치되거나 보류된 적이 없는 새로운 문제입니다.

## 변경 내역

### 1. PubSub 재연결 시 경합 조건으로 인한 연결 누수 방지

**파일:** `modules/tasks/src/database/pubsub.ts`

**문제:** `PostgresPubSub.connect()` 메서드에서, 연결이 끊어지면 `_onClosed` 핸들러가 `connect()`를 다시 호출합니다. 그런데 새로 획득한 연결의 `close` 이벤트가 `connect()` 완료 전에 발생하면, 두 개의 `connect()` 호출이 동시에 진행됩니다. 두 호출 모두 새 연결을 획득하지만 `this._connection`에는 마지막 연결만 저장되므로, 먼저 획득한 연결은 참조가 유실되어 정리되지 않습니다.

**근거:** `connect()` 메서드(라인 61-72)에서 `acquireRawConnection()` 후 `connection.on("close", this._onClosed)`를 즉시 등록합니다(라인 63). 새 연결이 불안정하여 즉시 닫히면, `_onClosed`가 현재 `connect()` 실행 중에 다시 호출됩니다. 두 호출이 각각 연결을 획득하고 `this._connection`에 덮어쓰면, 하나의 연결이 GC 대상이 될 때까지 열린 상태로 남습니다.

**수정:** `_connecting` 플래그를 추가하여, `connect()`가 이미 진행 중이면 후속 호출을 무시합니다. `try/finally`로 플래그를 안전하게 해제합니다.

**이렇게 하지 않으면:** 네트워크가 불안정한 환경에서 PubSub 재연결이 반복될 때, 정리되지 않는 PostgreSQL 연결이 누적되어 연결 풀이 고갈될 수 있습니다.

**영향:** `@sonamu-kit/tasks` 패키지의 PubSub 구독 기능. 정상적인 연결에서는 동작 변화가 없으며, 빠른 재연결이 필요한 불안정한 네트워크 환경에서만 차이가 발생합니다.

**확인 방법:** `pnpm --filter @sonamu-kit/tasks test` 실행 시 274개 전체 테스트 통과를 확인했습니다.

### 2. del() 메서드 문서의 반환값 설명 오류 수정

**파일:** `modules/docs/ko/api-reference/base-model/del.mdx`, `modules/docs/en/api-reference/base-model/del.mdx`

**문제:** 문서가 del() 메서드의 반환값을 "삭제된 레코드의 개수" / "count of deleted records"라고 설명하지만, 실제 구현은 `ids.length`(전달한 ID 배열의 길이)를 반환합니다. 예제 코드에서도 `del([1, 999, 1000])`의 반환값이 1이라고 표기하지만, 실제로는 3이 반환됩니다.

**근거:** `modules/sonamu/src/template/implementations/model.template.ts` 라인 194-203에서 del() 메서드 템플릿을 확인하면:
```typescript
async del(ids: ${idTsType}[]): Promise<number> {
    const wdb = this.getPuri("w");
    await wdb.transaction(async (trx) => {
      return trx.table("${entity.table}").whereIn("${entity.table}.id", ids).delete();
    });
    return ids.length;  // ← DB 삭제 결과가 아닌 ids.length 반환
}
```
`delete()` 호출의 반환값은 트랜잭션 내에서 사용되지 않고, 최종적으로 `ids.length`가 반환됩니다. 이는 의도된 동작입니다.

**수정 범위:**
- 반환값 설명: "삭제된 레코드의 개수" → "전달한 ID 배열의 길이(ids.length)"
- 존재하지 않는 ID 예제: 반환값 1 → 3으로 수정
- `count === 0` 기반 존재 확인 패턴: del([userId])는 항상 1을 반환하므로 동작하지 않음 → `findById`로 별도 확인하는 패턴으로 수정
- `count > 0` 기반 성공 확인 패턴: 동일한 이유로 수정
- 한국어/영어 문서 동시 수정

**이렇게 하지 않으면:** 개발자가 문서를 믿고 `count`를 실제 삭제 수로 사용하면, 존재하지 않는 ID를 포함한 삭제 요청에서 정확하지 않은 결과를 받게 됩니다. 특히 `count === 0`으로 존재 여부를 확인하는 패턴은 절대로 작동하지 않습니다(del([userId])는 항상 1을 반환).

**영향:** 문서 전용 변경이므로 런타임에 영향 없음.

**확인 방법:** 변경된 문서의 코드 예제가 `model.template.ts`의 실제 구현과 일치하는지 직접 대조하여 확인했습니다.

## 검토 필요 사항

- PubSub 수정이 기존 `pubsub.test.ts` 5건의 테스트를 모두 통과하지만, 실제 경합 조건을 재현하는 테스트는 추가하지 않았습니다. 네트워크 불안정 시뮬레이션이 필요한 통합 테스트의 필요 여부는 판단을 맡깁니다.

Summary:

Move cuptiActivityGetNumDroppedRecords() outside the mutex_ scope in
bufferCompleted(). When VLOG_IS_ON(1), this call re-enters CUPTI and needs
its internal rwlock, while bufferRequested() acquires mutex_ under that same
rwlock - creating a deadlock in multi-threaded environments (free-threaded
Python / no-GIL).

This follows the same pattern already used in activityBuffers() and
clearActivities(), which explicitly release mutex_ before CUPTI calls with
the comment: "Can't hold mutex_ during this call".

author: tulsi-builder
body:
## Overview

**Category:** new-feature
**User Impact:** Users can now see and select which AI model their provider uses, switch models or providers mid-conversation, and see a notification when the switch happens.

**Problem:** The model picker dropdown existed in the UI but was completely unpowered — it showed no models, couldn't be clicked, and changing providers mid-chat caused "Resource not found" errors from stale ACP session IDs.

**Solution:** Wire the existing dropdown to real model data from ACP providers (supporting both `SessionModelState` and `SessionConfigOption` paths), cache model lists in a shared store so navigation between Home and Chat is instant, and scope ACP session storage by provider to prevent cross-provider session reuse.

### Known limitations

- **Within-provider model switching is best-effort.** The ACP throwaway-process architecture means `set_model` can't reliably apply to an existing session. The user's model selection is stored and the pre-send sync attempts to apply it, but the provider may use its default. Cross-provider switching (Goose → Codex → Claude Code) works reliably.
- **Claude Code model discovery is slow (~60s).** This is due to ACP spawning a fresh process for each `acp_get_model_state` call. A potential fix is querying model state from the long-lived `AcpSessionRegistry` session instead of spawning throwaway processes — flagged for engineering input.
- **Model state is not persisted across app restarts.** `modelStateByProvider` is in-memory only. Each provider's models are re-fetched on first visit to the Home screen.

<details>
<summary>File changes</summary>

**src-tauri/src/services/acp/payloads.rs**
Added `AvailableModelPayload` and expanded `ModelStatePayload` to include `source`, `configId`, and `availableModels` fields.

**src-tauri/src/services/acp/writer.rs**
Emit model state from both `on_model_state_update` (SessionModelState) and `on_config_option_update` (SessionConfigOption with model category). Added normalization helpers for both paths.

**src-tauri/src/commands/acp.rs**
Added `acp_get_model_state` and `acp_set_model` Tauri commands. `acp_get_model_state` normalizes model state from either ACP path and falls back from `load_session` to `new_session` when stored session IDs are stale. Bootstrap no longer persists agent session IDs to avoid poisoning the send path.

**src-tauri/src/lib.rs**
Registered new `acp_get_model_state` and `acp_set_model` commands.

**src-tauri/src/services/acp/store.rs**
`TauriStore` now tracks `provider_id`. Cached agent session IDs are only returned when the stored provider matches, preventing cross-provider session reuse.

**src-tauri/src/services/acp/mod.rs**
Send path now passes provider ID to `TauriStore::with_provider` so session lookups are provider-scoped.

**src/shared/types/chat.ts**
Added `ModelOption`, `ModelSelectionSource`, and `ProviderModelState` types.

**src/shared/api/acp.ts**
Added `acpGetModelState` and `acpSetModel` frontend API wrappers.

**src/features/chat/stores/chatSessionStore.ts**
Added `modelStateByProvider` to store and `setModelState` action. `setModelState` preserves explicit user model selections when the provider reports a different default.

**src/features/chat/hooks/useAcpStream.ts**
Captures `acp:model_state` events and writes to the shared store.

**src/features/chat/hooks/useChat.ts**
Pre-send model sync attempts to apply the user's selected model before sending. Wrapped in try/catch so failures don't block the message.

**src/features/chat/ui/ChatView.tsx**
Bootstrap effect waits for `effectiveWorkingDir`, uses cached models from shared store when available, and avoids cascading re-fires. Model and provider switches inject system notifications. `currentModel` derivation simplified to a clear `useMemo` with explicit priority.

**src/features/chat/ui/ChatInput.tsx**
Accepts and passes through model picker props (`currentModel`, `currentModelId`, `modelsLoading`, `availableModels`, `onModelChange`).

**src/features/chat/ui/ChatInputToolbar.tsx**
Model dropdown renders from `availableModels`, shows loading state, and calls `onModelChange` on selection.

**src/features/home/ui/HomeScreen.tsx**
Model state reads/writes from shared `modelStateByProvider` store instead of local useState. Bootstrap writes to store so ChatView reads cached data on navigation.

**src/app/AppShell.tsx**
Passes model ID and name from Home screen into new chat session creation.

**src/app/hooks/useAppStartup.ts**
No functional change (pre-warm was added then reverted).

**scripts/check-file-sizes.mjs**
Added size exceptions for ChatView.tsx and acp.rs with justification.

**src/features/chat/ui/__tests__/ChatInput.test.tsx**
Added tests for model picker rendering, loading state, and selection callback.

**src/features/home/ui/HomeScreen.test.tsx**
Updated mock shapes for model bootstrap.

</details>

### Reproduction Steps

1. Start the app and navigate to the Home screen
2. Select a provider (Goose, Codex, or Claude Code) — model dropdown should populate after bootstrap
3. Select a model from the dropdown — label should update
4. Send a message — response should come from the selected provider
5. Switch providers mid-chat — "Switched to [Provider] ([Model])" notification should appear
6. Send another message — response should come from the new provider
7. Navigate from Home to Chat — model dropdown should populate instantly from cache (no "Loading models..." flash)

author: tgalloway1
body:
Deleted habits were invisible to goal progress for two reasons:
1. Entries were cascade-soft-deleted when a habit was deleted, making
   them invisible to goal queries that filter `deletedAt: { $exists: false }`
2. Goal progress computation skipped entries where the habit wasn't in
   the habitMap (`if (!habit) return sum` / `if (!habit) continue`)

Now:
- Habit deletion no longer cascade-soft-deletes entries (they persist
  as orphans, invisible in day view but queryable for goal aggregation)
- Entry repo functions accept `includeDeleted` option, used by goal
  progress queries to include legacy cascade-deleted entries
- Goal progress gracefully handles missing habits by using raw entry
  values instead of skipping them

Example: A "Run 100 miles" goal linked to a "Running" habit. User logs
50 miles, then deletes "Running" and creates "Trail Running". Previously
the goal showed 0 miles. Now correctly shows 50 miles.

body:
## Summary

This PR implements performance optimizations for the crates-docs MCP server, focusing on cache system efficiency and HTML processing performance.

## Changes

### 1. Cache System Optimization (`c474ad9`)
- **Problem**: `MemoryCache::get()` was cloning `String` on every cache hit, causing unnecessary memory allocation
- **Solution**: Changed internal storage from `String` to `Arc<String>`
  - `Cache` trait `get()` now returns `Option<Arc<String>>`
  - `MemoryCache` and `RedisCache` implementations updated
  - `DocCache` adapts at API boundary to maintain compatibility
- **Performance Impact**: Cache hits now only increment reference count instead of copying data

### 2. HTML Processing Optimization (`41b041c`)
- **Problem**: `remove_unwanted_elements()` used multiple `.replace()` calls, causing O(n²) complexity
- **Solution**: 
  - Sort elements by length (descending) to process parent elements before children
  - Extract regex patterns to separate function `apply_regex_patterns()`
  - Reduce string reconstruction overhead
- **Performance Impact**: Improved from O(n²) to approximately O(n)

### 3. Documentation Improvements (`16f326a`)
- Removed `#![allow(missing_docs)]` from:
  - `src/tools/docs/lookup_crate.rs`
  - `src/tools/docs/lookup_item.rs`
  - `src/tools/docs/search.rs`
  - `src/tools/health.rs`
- Added comprehensive documentation for all public types and functions
- Fixed doc comment placement issues

### 4. Code Review Fixes (`64a7c1d`)
- Fixed formatting issues in tests
- Corrected doc comment placement

| Formatting | ✅ Pass |

body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/kasianov-mikhail/scout/security/code-scanning/1](https://github.com/kasianov-mikhail/scout/security/code-scanning/1)

To fix this, explicitly declare `permissions` for the workflow so that the `GITHUB_TOKEN` has only the access needed. This workflow checks out the repository and runs local build/lint/test commands; that requires only read access to repository contents and does not need write access or other scopes.

The best fix is to add a `permissions:` block at the top (workflow) level, right after the `name:` or `on:` section, so it applies to all jobs (`lint` and `tests`) without changing their behavior. We should grant `contents: read` as the minimal required scope. No changes to steps, jobs, or external calls are needed.

Concretely, in `.github/workflows/swift.yml`, insert:

```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
```

between the `on:` block (lines 3–7) and the `concurrency:` block (line 9). This documents and enforces least privilege for the `GITHUB_TOKEN` used by both jobs.

### Before
```
name=cli-port-review	pid=40900	clients=0	created=1775160402	start_dir=/Users/...	cmd=bash -c...	ended=1775160877	exit_code=0
```

author: blakepettersson
body:
When normalizeTargetResources computes the live-to-target patch for RespectIgnoreDifferences, it uses strategic merge patch. For resources whose fields carry `patchStrategy:"replace"` (e.g. `policy/v1` PDB `spec.selector`), strategic merge treats the entire field as atomic — so patching in one ignored sub-field (say, a single `matchLabels` key) pulls the entire parent from the live object, overwriting non-ignored sibling fields that the user intentionally changed.

Add a post-correction step that walks the patched target against the original target and normalized target. If a field was not touched by the normalizer (`normalized == original`) but was overwritten by the patch (`patched != original`), restore the original target value. This surgically undoes collateral damage from replace semantics without affecting array merge behavior.

Currently only `policy/v1` PDB `spec.selector` uses `patchStrategy:"replace"` among built-in types, but the fix is generic and will also cover CRDs with `x-kubernetes-patch-strategy: replace` when OpenAPI-based patching is re-introduced. Fixes #18232.

author: copilot
body:
`sigma list targets` and `sigma list pipelines` exposed backend/pipeline identifiers with no way to trace them back to the installed plugin. This made it impossible to programmatically determine which plugin to uninstall (e.g., `elasticsearch` installs `lucene`, `eql`, `esql`, `elastalert` — none of which map back to `elasticsearch` in the list output).

## Changes

- **`sigma/cli/list.py`**
  - Added `_plugin_id_from_module()` — extracts the Sigma plugin identifier from a module name by reading the namespace component (e.g. `sigma.backends.splunk.backend` → `splunk`)
  - Added `_get_backend_plugin_id()` and `_get_pipeline_plugin_id()` — resolve a backend class or pipeline callable/instance to its Sigma plugin identifier; handles `@Pipeline`-decorated instances via the `.func` attribute
  - Pre-computes `_pipeline_plugin_ids` at module load time before the pipeline resolver discards callable/module metadata
  - Added **"Plugin"** column to both `list_targets` and `list_pipelines` table output showing the Sigma plugin identifier (e.g. `splunk`, `elasticsearch`, `windows`)

- **`tests/test_lists.py`**
  - Added `test_targets_has_plugin_column` and `test_pipelines_has_plugin_column` verifying the column header is present and no `n/a` values appear when plugins are installed

## Example output

```
$ sigma list targets
+-------------------------+-----------------------+------------------------------+---------------+
| Identifier              | Target Query Language | Processing Pipeline Required | Plugin        |
+-------------------------+-----------------------+------------------------------+---------------+
| lucene                  | Lucene                | No                           | elasticsearch |
| eql                     | EQL                   | No                           | elasticsearch |
+-------------------------+-----------------------+------------------------------+---------------+

$ sigma list pipelines
+-------------------+----------+-------------------------+-------------+---------------+
| Identifier        | Priority | Processing Pipeline     | Backends    | Plugin        |
+-------------------+----------+-------------------------+-------------+---------------+
| ecs_windows       | 20       | ECS Windows             | lucene, eql | elasticsearch |
+-------------------+----------+-------------------------+-------------+---------------+
```

body:
`warnings.warn` is routinely suppressed in production, making IP enrichment, geo lookup, and `get_logger` parameter ambiguity failures silently swallowed.

## Changes

- **`visionlog/enrichers/network.py`**: Swap `import warnings` for a module-level `_logger = logging.getLogger("visionlog")`; replace both `warnings.warn(...)` calls with `_logger.warning(...)` using `%s` format args (avoids eager string interpolation)
- **`visionlog/visionlog.py`**: Remove inline `import warnings`; replace the ambiguous-parameter warning with `logging.getLogger("visionlog").warning(...)` (stdlib `logging` was already imported)
- **Tests**: Update affected tests to mock `visionlog.enrichers.network._logger` and assert via `mock_logger.warning.assert_called_once()` instead of `warnings.catch_warnings`

## Before / After

```python
# Before
except (...) as error:
    warnings.warn(f"Failed to fetch public IP: {error}")

# After
except (...) as error:
    _logger.warning("Failed to fetch public IP: %s", error)
```

Failures now surface through the standard logging pipeline regardless of warning filters.

## Summary

`load_config_dict()` calls `AutoConfig.from_pretrained()` without `trust_remote_code`, so `build_hf_model(..., trust_remote_code=True)` fails for models with custom HF code (Kimi K2, Kimi K2.5, Nemotron) when the model isn't already cached locally.

The fix forwards the already-resolved `trust_remote_code` from `build_hf_model` to `load_config_dict`.

**Affected models:** Kimi-K2-Thinking, Kimi-K2.5, NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16 (any model with custom `modeling_*.py` in its HF repo).

**Note:** When model weights are already cached locally, `load_config_dict` reads `config.json` directly from disk and never hits `AutoConfig`, so the bug only manifests on first use before the model is cached.

author: angus-langchain
body:
## Summary

- Adds `set_metadata()` method to `OtelSpanProcessor` that propagates `langsmith.metadata.*` attributes to OTEL spans.
- Fixes a tracing issue where OTel-based frameworks only set `thread_id` on the root span, causing LangSmith's thread view to show 0 tokens

## Example usage

```python
from opentelemetry import trace
from langsmith.integrations.otel.processor import OtelSpanProcessor

# Get your existing TracerProvider (e.g. set up by CrewAI)
provider = trace.get_tracer_provider()

# Add LangSmith processor with thread_id propagation
processor = OtelSpanProcessor(project="my-project")
processor.set_metadata({"thread_id": "conversation-123"})
provider.add_span_processor(processor)

# Update thread_id for a new conversation
processor.set_metadata({"thread_id": "conversation-456"})
```

author: nomiscz
body:
## What is this PR about? ### Summary: Fix `TypeError: isDate is not a function` in [Drop Deployment](https://docs.dokploy.com/docs/core/providers#drag-and-drop-zip-applications) by upgrading ssh2 from 1.15.0 to ^1.16.0, which replaces the removed util.isDate with util.types.isDate for Node.js v23+ compatibility. ### Description: `ssh2@1.15.0` imports `isDate` directly from Node.js's `util` module. However, `isDate` was deprecated and removed in Node.js v23+. ```js const { inherits, isDate } = require('util'); ``` ssh2 commit: https://github.com/mscdex/ssh2/commit/4f771c92daab356afbe56f0a40ea2a540b0b6beb Dokploy now requires `"node": "^24.4.0"`, which means util.isDate destructures as undefined at runtime. When the bundled code calls isDate(attrs.atime) during an SFTP file upload, it throws: ``` TypeError: isDate is not a function at (.next/server/chunks/1568.js:1022:19071) at new Promise () ``` Called API endpoint: `/api/trpc/application.dropDeployment`: ```json { "error": { "json": { "message": "isDate is not a function", "code": -32603, "data": { "code": "INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR", "httpStatus": 500, "path": "application.dropDeployment", "zodError": null } } } } ``` This breaks the [Drop Deployment feature](https://docs.dokploy.com/docs/core/providers#drag-and-drop-zip-applications) — every file upload via SFTP fails with HTTP 500. ## Checklist Before submitting this PR, please make sure that: - [X] You created a dedicated branch based on the `canary` branch. - [X] You have read the suggestions in the CONTRIBUTING.md file https://github.com/Dokploy/dokploy/blob/canary/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-request - [X] You have tested this PR in your local instance. If you have not tested it yet, please do so before submitting. This helps avoid wasting maintainers' time reviewing code that has not been verified by you. ## Screenshots (if applicable)

Greptile Summary

This PR fixes a runtime crash in the Drop Deployment (`.zip` upload) feature by upgrading `ssh2` from `1.15.0` to `^1.16.0` (resolves to `1.17.0` in the lockfile). The root cause is that Node.js v23+ removed `util.isDate`, which `ssh2@1.15.0` destructures directly from `require('util')`. Since Dokploy now requires Node.js `^24.4.0`, this caused every SFTP file upload to throw `TypeError: isDate is not a function` and return HTTP 500. The upgrade to `ssh2@1.17.0` uses `util.types.isDate` instead, restoring compatibility. Key changes: - `packages/server/package.json`: `ssh2` bumped from pinned `1.15.0` to `^1.16.0` - `pnpm-lock.yaml`: Resolves `ssh2` to `1.17.0` and includes expected collateral lockfile changes (peer-dependency hash updates for `better-auth`, `jiti` minor resolution shifts for dev/test tooling). None of these collateral changes affect production runtime behavior.

Confidence Score: 5/5

This PR is safe to merge — it is a minimal, well-scoped dependency bump that directly addresses a confirmed production crash on Node.js v23+. The fix is precise and well-justified: ssh2@1.17.0 contains the exact upstream commit that replaces the removed util.isDate with util.types.isDate. The change is isolated to one dependency. The collateral lockfile changes (better-auth hash updates, jiti version swaps in dev/test tooling snapshots) are normal artifacts of lockfile regeneration and carry no production risk. No breaking changes are introduced by the ssh2 minor version upgrade. No files require special attention. author: gregorycomer
body:
Add scalar kernels for bf16 minmax. This is needed for dynamic quantization. I followed the same pattern as the existing f16 minmax kernels using math_signcomplement_f16 and integer comparison. I generate the same set of min, max, and minmax kernels as f16 and use the same kernel selection pattern.

This is a large-ish PR due to the number of generated kernels. Feel free to let me know if you'd prefer I split this up or reduce the number of generated kernels.

## Benchmarks
Mostly just sanity checking to make sure there's no regression over f16. I didn't run a ton of iterations, so it's a little noisy, but shows that the bf16 ones are sane. I've included f32 for reference. Interestingly, f32 scalars seem to be a bit slower than f16 (note that the benchmarks are already in GiB/s). Maybe because it's not using the bit inversion trick?

### M4 Max

 | GiB/s | bf16 scalar | f16 scalar | f16 NEON | f32 scalar | f32 NEON |
  |--|-------------|------------|----------|------------|----------|
  | rmax | 41.4 | 44.0 | 61.1 | 13.9 | 78.1 |
  | rmin | 43.4 | 41.6 | 64.1 | 13.6 | 80.9 |
  | rminmax | 36.0 | 35.7 | 57.6 | 13.4 | 69.1 |

### Cortex X1 (Pixel 7 Pro)

| GiB/s | bf16 scalar | f16 scalar | f16 NEON | f32 scalar | f32 NEON |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | rmax | 22.7 | 21.8 | 39.5 | 6.7 | 32.2 |
  | rmin | 22.4 | 21.5 | 39.1 | 6.7 | 32.5 |
  | rminmax | 18.9 | 18.0 | 34.7 | 4.9 | 32.9 |

### Broadwell

| GiB/s | bf16 scalar | f16 scalar | f32 scalar | f32 AVX |
  |--|-------------|------------|------------|---------|
  | rmax | 2.79 | 2.64 | 10.74 | 21.98 |

Managed as a singleton via `App.getBfdClientService()` to avoid expensive per-request `FhirContext` creation. Implements `Closeable` to properly release the underlying `CloseableHttpClient`. All four search methods (`getEobsByPatient`, `getCoverageByPatient`, `getClaimByPatient`, `getClaimResponseByPatient`) follow `Bundle.LINK_NEXT` pagination.
- `BfdConfiguration` — Environment-variable-driven config (`BFD_SERVER_URL`, cert/key/truststore paths, separate client key password)
- `BfdToPasTransformer` — Maps BFD Patient/EOB/Coverage → PAS Claim bundles (handles all 8 EOB claim types)
- `PasToBfdTransformer` — Maps PAS ClaimResponse dispositions → BFD-compatible EOB extensions with X12 review action codes

**New endpoint**:
- `PatientPriorAuthEndpoint` — `GET /PriorAuthorization?patient={mbi}` returns a Bundle of ClaimResponses for a given Medicare Beneficiary Identifier

**Modified existing code**:
- `App` — Initializes singleton `BfdClientService` at startup via `initializeBfdClient()`; exposes via `getBfdClientService()`
- `ClaimEndpoint` — Adds non-blocking BFD patient validation on `$submit` (with null-patient guard)
- `Database` — Adds configurable PostgreSQL support alongside existing H2 (via `DB_TYPE`, `DB_URL`, `DB_USER`, `DB_PASSWORD` env vars)
- `ClaimResponseFactory` — Caches `requestMappingTable.json` at startup instead of re-reading on every call
- `Metadata` — Adds PAS/CARIN profiles and patient search param to the `ClaimResponse` CapabilityStatement entry
- `build.gradle` — Adds PostgreSQL JDBC driver and `hapi-fhir-client` dependency

**Documentation**: BFD data analysis, BFD→PAS field mappings, CMS-0057-F compliance checklist, validation script.

### Updates since last revision (Devin Review round 1 — commit `6bc9b95`)

Five bugs fixed:

1. **Database.java — `SELECT TOP 1` is H2-specific** (CRITICAL): Added conditional logic checking `dbType` to emit `LIMIT 1` for PostgreSQL vs `SELECT TOP 1` for H2 in both `read()` and `readString()`.
2. **BfdClientService.java — Global `FhirContext` modification** (MEDIUM): Created a dedicated `bfdFhirContext = FhirContext.forR4()` instance so BFD client settings no longer mutate the application-wide singleton.
3. **BfdClientService.java — mTLS `SSLContext` never applied** (CRITICAL): `SSLContext` is now applied to a custom `CloseableHttpClient` via `HttpClients.custom().setSSLContext(sslContext)`, set on the `RestfulClientFactory` before creating the FHIR generic client.
4. **BfdToPasTransformer.java — Incorrect EOB type code mappings** (CRITICAL): Removed invalid codes 72/81. All 8 BFD claim types now correctly mapped: 60/40/20/10/50 → institutional, 71/82 → professional, PDE → pharmacy.
5. **PatientPriorAuthEndpoint.java — XML handler returns JSON** (MEDIUM): Added `RequestType` parameter so XML requests use `FhirUtils.getFormattedData()` with the correct `MediaType`.

### Updates since last revision (Devin Review round 2 — commit `82405ea`)

Four additional bugs fixed:

1. **Database.java — `datetime` type not converted for PostgreSQL** (CRITICAL): `adaptSqlForPostgresql()` now converts `datetime` → `timestamp`. Without this, all 8 `CREATE TABLE` statements in `CreateDatabase.sql` would fail on PostgreSQL.
2. **BfdToPasTransformer.java — `extractMbi` returns non-MBI identifiers** (CRITICAL): Removed the `bene_id` fallback (which returned internal numeric BFD IDs labeled as MBI) and the generic first-identifier fallback. Now only returns values from known MBI system URIs (`us-mbi`, `us-medicare`); returns `null` otherwise.
3. **PasToBfdTransformerTest.java — `testMapNullDisposition` fails** (MEDIUM): Test asserted `assertNotNull` but `mapDispositionToAdjudicationCategory(null)` returns `null`. Changed to `assertNull`.
4. **Metadata.java — Duplicate `ClaimResponse` in CapabilityStatement** (MEDIUM): Both `getClaimResponse()` and `getPriorAuthorization()` declared type `"ClaimResponse"`, producing an invalid CapabilityStatement. Merged PAS/CARIN profiles and patient search param into the existing `getClaimResponse()` method and removed the separate `getPriorAuthorization()` method.

### Updates since last revision (Devin Review round 3 — commit `7a57e6b`)

Two bugs fixed:

1. **BfdClientService per-request instantiation causing performance degradation and resource leak** (CRITICAL): `BfdClientService` was instantiated per-request in both `ClaimEndpoint.validateAndEnrichWithBfd()` and `PatientPriorAuthEndpoint.fetchBfdPatient()`, creating a new `FhirContext.forR4()`, SSL context, and `CloseableHttpClient` on every call — with the `CloseableHttpClient` never closed. Fixed by:
   - Making `BfdClientService` a singleton initialized once at startup in `App.initializeBfdClient()`
   - Both endpoints now use `App.getBfdClientService()` (returns `null` if BFD is not enabled)
   - `BfdClientService` implements `Closeable`; the `httpClient` is stored as an instance field and properly closed in `close()`
2. **`validateAndEnrichWithBfd` called before null check on patient** (MEDIUM): In `processBundle()`, `validateAndEnrichWithBfd(claim, patient)` was called at line 269 before the null check on `patient` at line 285. When `getPatientIdentifierFromBundle()` returns null (malformed bundle), this would cause a `NullPointerException` in `BfdClientService.getPatientByMbi()` at `mbi.substring()`. Added `if (patient != null)` guard.

### Updates since last revision (Devin Review round 4 — commit `7a55e8a`)

Three bugs fixed:

1. **BfdConfiguration.java — Client PKCS12 keystore password not configurable** (CRITICAL): `buildSslContext()` used `trustStorePassword` for both the client PKCS12 keystore (`keyStore.load()`, `keyManagerFactory.init()`) and the JKS trust store. In production mTLS deployments these typically have different passwords, causing `UnrecoverableKeyException` or `IOException` with no way to configure the correct client key password. Fixed by adding a dedicated `clientKeyPassword` field (read from `BFD_CLIENT_KEY_PASSWORD` env var, defaulting to `trustStorePassword` for backward compatibility). Updated both constructors, added getter, and updated `application.properties`.
2. **PatientPriorAuthEndpoint.java — 400 error response hardcodes JSON format** (MEDIUM): The missing-patient error path used `FhirUtils.json(error)` and `MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON`, ignoring the `requestType` parameter. XML clients requesting via `getPriorAuthorizationsXml()` would receive JSON error responses. Now uses `FhirUtils.getFormattedData(error, requestType)` with conditional `MediaType`.
3. **PatientPriorAuthEndpoint.java — 500 error response hardcodes JSON format** (MEDIUM): Same issue in the catch block. Now uses the same content-negotiation pattern as the success response path and `ClaimEndpoint.java`.

### Updates since last revision (Devin Review round 5 — commit `ab0dccf`)

One bug fixed:

1. **PatientPriorAuthEndpointTest.java — `@TestPropertySource` auth bypass is ineffective** (MEDIUM): The test set `BYPASS_AUTH=true` via `@TestPropertySource`, but `AuthUtils.validateAccessToken()` reads from `System.getenv("BYPASS_AUTH")` — an OS environment variable unaffected by Spring's `@TestPropertySource`. No test requests included an `Authorization` header either, so all tests would receive HTTP 401 instead of the expected 200/400. Fixed by adding `.header("Authorization", "Bearer Y3YWq2l08kvFqy50fQJY")` to all 5 test methods (matching the pattern in `ClaimSubmitTest`) and removing the ineffective `BYPASS_AUTH=true` from `@TestPropertySource`.

### Updates since last revision (Devin Review round 6 — commit `d9b686b`)

Two bugs fixed:

## Summary

Ground-up rewrite of the Claude Code Framework as **Vibe Framework v3.0**. Persistent `.vibe/` project context, auto-generated `debug/` test harness, and disciplined subagent-orchestrated workflows.

### What's New
- **13 commands** (was 11): init, plan, go, tdd, oneshot, ralph, review, commit, ask, note, add, refresh, help
- **`.vibe/` structure**: understanding.md, current.md, bugs.md, risks.md, future.md, decisions.md, docs/
- **`debug/` test harness**: auto-generated, maintained by all workflows, gates commits
- **Bug/risk tracking**: sequential IDs (#1, #R1) with CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW impact levels
- **Decision tracking**: [USER] and [CLAUDE] tags with assumption lifecycle
- **Two-stage review**: spec compliance first, then code quality (from superpowers patterns)
- **4-state agent output**: DONE / DONE_WITH_CONCERNS / BLOCKED / NEEDS_CONTEXT
- **3-fix rule**: engineer escalates after 3 failed attempts
- **Plan mode**: EnterPlanMode for brainstorming, prevents accidental code writes
- **Hooks**: session-end warning for active tasks
- **Context7 + WebSearch fallback chain** for API verification

### What Changed
- Commands trimmed 22% (1,362 → 1,060 lines) while adding features
- Agents reduced to 15-25 lines each (shared behavior in vibe-context skill)
- Pre-compute bash blocks fixed: test detection chain, playwright detection syntax
- Removed: learn, log, risks, status commands (functionality absorbed into new commands)
- Removed: codebase-context skill (replaced by vibe-context with role-based loading)

### Attribution
Originally created by Jack Lutz. This rewrite extends the framework significantly while preserving the core philosophy: plan before coding, verify your work, build persistent context.

### Install

**From this fork (dukesmith0):**
```bash
claude plugin marketplace add dukesmith0/vibe-framework
claude plugin install vibe@vibe-marketplace
```

**From original repo (jwlutz) — if this PR is merged:**
```bash
claude plugin marketplace add jwlutz/claude_code_framework
claude plugin install vibe@vibe-marketplace
```

author: osortega
body:
## Problem

When a new agent session is created and a chat is sent, two entries briefly appear in the session list — the temporary "New Session..." entry and the real committed session — before the temp one disappears.

## Root Cause

In `_sendFirstChat` (and `_sendSubsequentChat`), after `sendRequest()` returns, the code always calls `_waitForCommittedSession()` which listens for the `onDidCommitSession` IPC event to get the committed URI. However, `sendRequest()` already returns the committed URI synchronously as `result.newSessionResource`.

Meanwhile, `agentSessionsService.model.onDidChangeSessions` fires as soon as the agent model is updated, causing `_refreshSessionCache` to add the real `AgentSessionAdapter` to the cache — making the real session appear in the UI. But the temp session isn't removed until `_waitForCommittedSession` resolves from the later IPC event, creating a window where both entries are visible.

## Fix

Both `_sendFirstChat` and `_sendSubsequentChat` now use `result.newSessionResource` directly when available, falling back to `_waitForCommittedSession()` only when it is not set. This eliminates the duplicate entry flicker by skipping the unnecessary async wait.

author: philoserf
body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

body:
## Summary

Comprehensive security hardening across the entire platform, implementing 8 phases from the codebase review:

- **Permission enforcement** on all 164 server actions via `assertPermission()` + `requireSchoolContext()`
- **Tenant isolation** — replaced `db.school.findFirst()` with session-based `schoolId` across all actions
- **PostgreSQL Row-Level Security** — 173 RLS policies on all tenant-scoped tables, with `withTenant()` helper
- **Schema hardening** — added `schoolId` to 79 child tables with backfill migration
- **Redis-backed rate limiting** with in-memory fallback
- **Receipt number race condition fix** using PostgreSQL sequences
- **Audit logging** — retry logic, `schoolId` tracking
- **Frontend** — discriminated union narrowing fixes across 289 files, ErrorBoundary, focus trap, aria-live, shared types

### Key metrics
| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Files changed | 513 |
| Actions with permission checks | 158/164 (6 exempt: login, public, portal) |
| RLS policies | 173 tables |
| TypeScript errors | 0 |
| Tests passing | 1280/1280 |

## Test plan

body:
## Summary
- Add detailed commit summary to auto-release PR description
- Add collapsible commit list
- Add files changed count
- Add update timestamp

## Problem
PR #235 (Release PR) shows minimal description that never updates:

```markdown
## ✅ Pre-deployment Checklist

- [ ] All CI checks passing
- [ ] Tests passing
- [ ] No breaking changes
- [ ] Ready for production

---
*🤖 Auto-generated release PR*
```

**Root cause:**
1. `auto-release-pr.yml` only generates minimal checklist (lines 61-71)
2. Comment says "detailed analysis will be added by pr-description.yml"
3. But `pr-description.yml` only triggers on `pull_request: [opened, synchronize]`
4. When new commits merge to develop, PR #235 doesn't get `synchronize` event
5. Result: PR #235 description never updates with new commits

## Solution
Generate detailed release notes directly in `auto-release-pr.yml`:

**Added:**
- Total commits count
- Collapsible commit list (all commits from main..develop)
- Files changed count  
- Update timestamp

**Example output:**
```markdown
## ✅ Pre-deployment Checklist
...

## 📝 Changes Summary

**Total commits**: 15

<details>
<summary>📋 Commit List</summary>

- abc1234 feat: Add feature X
- def5678 fix: Fix bug Y
...

</details>

## 📁 Files Changed

**Total files changed**: 42

---
*🤖 Auto-generated release PR - Updated: 2026-04-03 12:34:56 UTC*
```

## Benefits
✅ PR #235 will show all commits being released
✅ Timestamp shows when description was last updated
✅ Better visibility into release contents
✅ No dependency on pr-description.yml for release PRs

- [x] Pre-commit hooks passed
- [ ] Merge to develop
- [ ] Wait for auto-release-pr workflow to run
- [ ] Verify PR #235 description updates with detailed release notes
